# Architecture reference 01

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## 1. Document control and reading guide

- Revision: 2026-10-23.
- Status: design baseline for implementation; not a description of a production system.
- Audience: backend, web, mobile, operations, QA, security reviewers, and maintainers.
- Product: HRFlow is a placeholder name for a multi-tenant HR platform.
- Delivery constraint: twelve weeks, contributor A on backend/web/infrastructure and B on Flutter.
- Authoritative contracts: [API, persistence, and events](../REST-API-DATABASE-DESIGN.md).
- Authoritative delivery sequence: [execution plan](../PLAN.md).
- Historical reconnaissance: [project analysis](../PROJECT-ANALYSIS.md), a dated snapshot rather than the current contract.

### 1.1 Status vocabulary

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Implemented | Verified source or configuration exists; runtime readiness is stated separately |
| Partial | Some code/configuration exists but the capability is incomplete |
| Planned | Existing project documents establish intended behavior; implementation is absent |
| Proposed | Recommendation introduced by this specification; not an approved product decision |
| Unknown | Evidence or an external decision is missing |

Sections describing runtime behavior below are **planned design**, unless explicitly labeled implemented. Examples, limits, schemas, and new endpoint extensions are **proposed contracts** until reviewed and implemented. An ADR marked Proposed records a recommendation, not approval.

### 1.2 Evidence and conflict resolution

Current behavior is established by source/configuration, then migrations/tests. Intended behavior comes from requirements and the pre-existing plan/API draft, then recorded ADRs. Accidental scaffold behavior does not silently replace a business requirement. This document records discrepancies and a disposition rather than claiming they are fixed. No application dependencies, infrastructure definitions, or business code were changed for this specification.

### 1.3 Repository baseline

| Component | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Seven Java services | `services/*/src/main/java` contains application entry points only | Partial |
| Root reactor | `pom.xml`, seven service modules, two libraries | Implemented configuration |
| Event library | `libs/hrflow-event-starter` dependencies and Kafka YAML, no Java classes | Partial |
| Event contracts | One Avro check-in record in `libs/hrflow-contracts/events` | Partial |
| Attendance persistence | Datasource/JPA/Flyway YAML, no entities or migrations | Partial |
| Business REST APIs | No controllers/DTOs/security policies found | Planned |
| Nuxt web | `web/app/app.vue` renders Nuxt welcome | Partial |
| Flutter | No source found in repository | Planned; external repository unknown |
| Confidence scoring | FastAPI, rules, training, model artifact, five tests | Implemented standalone prototype |
| Local dependencies | PostgreSQL/Kafka/UI/Registry Compose | Partial; configuration defects remain |
| Deployment/CI | No Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, or workflow files | Planned |
| API/design contracts | Markdown specification in this suite | Planned; not generated implementation |

### 1.4 Verified discrepancies and disposition

| ID | Finding | Disposition; implementation task |
|---|---|---|
| D01 | Root Boot parent 4.1.1; services independently use 4.0.8 | Align parent inheritance/version in week 1; no upgrade prescribed |
| D02 | Plan previously said Boot 3 | Source establishes current Boot 4 configuration; remove stale intended-version claim |
| D03 | React plan; Nuxt 4.6.1/Vue source | Preserve scaffold; propose Nuxt for MVP, decision O01 |
| D04 | Attendance port 8082; API draft 8102 | 8101–8106 remain target service ports; config correction pending |
| D05 | API draft schema `identity`; init creates `identity_org` | Canonical target is `identity_org`, consistent with bootstrap |
| D06 | Six YAML resources contain `spring.application.name=...` | Convert to YAML mappings before service startup |
| D07 | PostgreSQL SQL mount repeats `infra/docker` relative path | Correct mount relative to Compose file before fresh initialization |
| D08 | Registry points to `kafka:19092`; listener is 29092 | Use declared internal listener; verify readiness |
| D09 | Avro plugin points at absent root `contracts/events` | Correct to library's `events` directory before generation |
| D10 | No service imports shared libraries | Wire starter only after its auto-configuration and tests exist |
| D11 | Original “all writes return 202” rule | Synchronous durable writes use 200/201; exports/year-end jobs use 202 |
| D12 | Universal employee Kafka key | Use aggregate keys for shifts, holidays, requests; see section 13 |
| D13 | “Never delete” versus privacy retention | No normal business deletion of evidence; controlled retention erasure remains required |
| D14 | Manual always wins versus holiday/leave precedence | Separate evidence from classification; unresolved policy O02 blocks automatic conflict resolution |
| D15 | Reporting balance endpoint lacks source event | Propose `leave.balance.v1`; no cross-schema query fallback |
| D16 | Notification called command-free but has preferences/device/read commands | It owns notification-specific commands, not HR workflow decisions |

The original empty `Achitecture.MD` was corrected to `Architecture.md` to match the requested canonical deliverable. The API/database draft already had meaningful coverage at this revision; it was preserved and normalized.

## 2. System overview and domain

### 2.1 Goals and non-goals

Employees use mobile self-service to record attendance and submit requests. Managers review direct-report attendance and approve assigned decisions. HR configures organization data, policies, corrections, and exports. The design favors a durable check-in even when notifications are unavailable. Auditability, tenant separation, and recoverable asynchronous work are core requirements. Payroll, recruitment, continuous GPS tracking, authoritative warehouse inventory, and facial identification are outside MVP scope. Camera evidence remains an optional future proposal; its presence in an old enum does not establish permission to collect it.

```text
flowchart LR
  E[Employee] --> M[Flutter mobile - planned]
  H[HR and manager] --> W[Web - Nuxt scaffold]
  M --> G[API gateway - partial]
  W --> G
  G --> S[Domain services - scaffolds]
  S --> P[(PostgreSQL service schemas - planned tables)]
  S --> K[Kafka - local configuration]
  K --> R[Notification and reporting - planned consumers]
  R --> X[FCM and email - planned]
```


### 2.2 Actors and authorization scope

| Actor | Responsibilities | Resource scope |
|---|---|---|
| EMPLOYEE | Attendance, own leave/requests/preferences | Own linked employee only |
| MANAGER | Team views and assigned approvals | Current direct reports; no implicit tenant-wide access |
| HR_ADMIN | Tenant organization, policies, authorized corrections/reports | Own tenant |
| OWNER | Tenant settings and audit review | Own tenant; HR capabilities require explicit HR grant |
| Platform operator | Provision/suspend tenants, key/deployment operations | Separate control-plane credential; not an OWNER role |
| Background worker | Cutoff, relay, export, provider delivery | Explicit tenant and job scope |

A role is necessary but insufficient: every object operation also checks ownership, current manager relationship, assigned step, and tenant. No approver may approve their own request; escalation goes to a different HR administrator. The platform provisioning API is not available to ordinary tenant access tokens.

### 2.3 Domain vocabulary and lifecycle

A **user** is a login identity; an **employee** is an employment record, optionally linked to one user in the tenant. A **work site** defines approved nudge/evidence context, not proof of human presence. A **shift** is a local-time schedule; an **assignment** applies it over effective dates. A **work date** is the local date on which the assigned shift starts. **Evidence** records an observation with provenance; it is not an attendance conclusion. A **session** records an interpreted working interval and source. A **correction** requests or records a new interpretation without deleting prior evidence. A **daily status** is a recalculable projection of calendar, leave, and effective sessions. A **revision** is a monotonic aggregate version, not a wall-clock timestamp.

Employee lifecycle: provision → assign schedule → activate → update/transfer → terminate. Termination revokes refresh sessions, prevents new self-service commands, and publishes a full employee snapshot. Downstream historical records remain; future cutoff jobs exclude terminated employees from their effective termination date. Tenant lifecycle is ACTIVE → SUSPENDED → controlled closure; suspension blocks normal login and mutations. Deletion is an administrative retention workflow, not a cascade that silently removes HR history.

Attendance lifecycle: evidence → open session → checkout or missing-checkout review → effective revision → daily recomputation. Inference adds a pending-confirmation interpretation; rejection excludes it from worked-time totals. Leave lifecycle: PENDING → APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED; APPROVED may become NEEDS_REVIEW after attendance conflict. General request lifecycle: DRAFT → PENDING → APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED → FULFILLED when applicable. Notification lifecycle: accepted event → durable inbox/notification → delivery attempts → provider acceptance/failure. Reporting lifecycle: consume fact → guarded upsert → freshness watermark → query/export → retention cleanup.

### 2.4 Business invariants

- All tenant business objects and commands have one trusted tenant context.
- One employee has at most one open effective session; multiple closed sessions per work date are permitted.
- A session's checkout cannot precede check-in.
- The client cannot declare itself an HR actor or select a different employee for self-service.
- Leave availability is entitlement plus carry-over minus used minus pending reservation.
- Balance reservations and request transitions commit together in the leave database.
- Approval transitions check current state and version in the same transaction.
- Business mutation and publication intent commit atomically in the owner database.
- Historical evidence and decision actions are append-only in normal application flows.
- Projection freshness is visible; asynchronous projections do not pretend to be immediately authoritative.

## 3. Quality attributes and acceptance targets

These are proposed acceptance targets, not production guarantees. No uptime commitment or capacity guarantee has been established.

| Attribute | Target or invariant | Measurement and validation |
|---|---|---|
| Check-in latency | p95 <150 ms | Gateway receive to response complete; same-region warm services, 100 concurrent clients; include DB/outbox commit, exclude device network |
| Tail latency | Record p99, no numerical promise yet | Same histogram/window as p95; retain error and timeout samples separately |
| Dashboard propagation | p95 <2 s | Source commit time to visible projection/SSE render; clocks synchronized; report consumer and UI portions |
| Load | 100 concurrent check-ins, zero unexplained errors | Distinct employees plus duplicate-key cases; dataset and hardware recorded |
| Isolation | Zero cross-tenant disclosure or mutation | Two-tenant API/repository/event/export fixtures, ID substitution and role tests |
| Reliability | No acknowledged command lost after tested restart | DB durability + outbox/inbox crash tests; compare resource/event IDs |
| Auditability | Every privileged decision has actor/reason/time | Contract and transaction assertions for approvals/corrections/adjustments |
| Recovery | Recover stopped notification consumer | Stop, check in, restart, observe one in-app notification and caught-up offsets |
| Repeatability | Fresh checkout can reproduce demo | Pinned toolchain, migrations, documented setup and seeded non-sensitive data |
| Cost | Original `$`30 budget alert retained as proposal | Alert threshold is not a cost estimate; forecast compute/database/broker/egress before deployment |
| Adoption | Manual check-in rate ≥70% | Pilot denominator = eligible scheduled days, excluding leave/holidays |
| Inference | Recover ≥90% forgotten days within ±10 min | Separate labeled pilot evaluation; not a launch claim or synthetic metric |
| Battery | <3% added workday battery use | Compare permitted nudge mode with baseline on representative Android/iOS devices |

Availability is tracked initially as successful eligible requests divided by eligible requests in the pilot window. Exclude deliberate maintenance only when disclosed; do not remove dependency failures from error rates. Define a production SLO and error budget after workload and operational ownership are known. Failure of a performance target triggers profiling and scope review, not removal of correctness checks.

## 4. Architectural style and service boundaries

### 4.1 Decision baseline

The existing plan establishes domain-oriented services, Kafka-only business integration, local projections, and service-owned schemas. These are intended architecture, not implemented runtime guarantees. [ADR-001](../adr/001-SERVICE-AND-EVENT-BOUNDARIES.md) records that baseline and proposed delivery safeguards. One physical PostgreSQL instance is an MVP cost simplification; schemas are not independent failure domains.

| Service | Owns | Must not own |
|---|---|---|
| api-gateway | Routes, edge authentication, limits, correlation | Leave balances, attendance decisions |
| identity-org | Tenant/user/org master data and token lifecycle | Other service tables |
| attendance | Evidence, sessions, corrections, statuses, cutoff | Authoritative identity or leave balances |
| leave | Policies, balances, requests, ledger | Attendance sessions |
| request | General requests, advisory materials, approval steps | Leave policies or inventory guarantees |
| notification | Preferences, inbox, device tokens, delivery | Business approval state |
| reporting | Derived facts, summaries, exports | Transactional HR truth |

### 4.2 Component view

```text
flowchart TB
  G[Gateway] --> I[identity-org]
  G --> A[attendance]
  G --> L[leave]
  G --> Q[request]
  G --> N[notification]
  G --> R[reporting]
  I --> O[Outbox and inbox library - planned]
  A --> O
  L --> O
  Q --> O
  O --> K[Kafka]
  K --> N
  K --> R
```


The shared starter contains infrastructure patterns, not shared domain entities or repositories. Each service performs its own authorization and transaction management. Gateway routing to domain APIs is an allowed synchronous client path. Business service-to-service HTTP and cross-service SQL joins are prohibited by the intended baseline. Infrastructure protocols to PostgreSQL/Kafka/storage and external provider calls are allowed. JWT signature verification uses cached JWKS; key discovery is a documented security-control-plane exception, not a synchronous business-data dependency.

### 4.3 Dependency view

```text
flowchart LR
  I[identity-org] -->|org snapshots| K[Kafka]
  L[leave] -->|leave requests and balances| K
  A[attendance] -->|sessions statuses conflicts| K
  Q[request] -->|workflow snapshots| K
  K -->|org and leave| A
  K -->|org and conflicts| L
  K -->|org| Q
  K -->|business facts| N[notification]
  K -->|facts and dimensions| R[reporting]
```


Local projections trade synchronous coupling for freshness and reconciliation work. The user-facing owner API returns authoritative local state immediately after commit. Read models may lag and must expose `asOf` and `projectionLagMs`. If org data needed for a command is missing, return retryable `REFERENCE_NOT_READY`; do not fabricate a shift.

### 5.1 Container and data ownership view

### 5.2 Trust boundaries

```text
flowchart LR
  U[Untrusted client and supplied headers] -->|TLS| E[Public edge]
  E -->|validated bearer token| G[Gateway]
  G -->|token forwarded and checked again| S[Private service network]
  S -->|service DB role| D[(Private PostgreSQL)]
```

Private networking reduces exposure but does not replace token verification or object authorization. Client-supplied tenant, employee, roles, and forwarded identity headers are removed at the edge. Background jobs derive tenant from a stored job or verified event, never from a thread-local leftover.

### 5.3 Local development view

```text
flowchart LR

  H -->|localhost 9092| K[Compose Kafka]
  H -->|localhost 8081| S[Compose Registry]
```

Compose currently includes no application containers and no automatic topic initialization. The broken SQL mount and Registry listener must be fixed before treating it as reproducible. The topic script creates six partitions per current topic, replication factor one, and compacted org topics. Local plaintext credentials and listeners are local-only defaults.

### 5.4 Production proposal

```text
flowchart TB
  B[Browser and mobile] --> T[TLS ingress]
  T --> G[Gateway containers]
  G --> S[Domain containers]
```

This is a logical production topology; no AWS or cluster resources exist in the repository. [ADR-005](../adr/005-DEPLOYMENT-AND-CLIENT-BASELINE.md) proposes a single-host/container pilot before Kubernetes. EKS versus k3s versus simple containers remains O04; EKS is not a mandatory MVP milestone. A single host and single broker have explicit downtime/data-loss risks and cannot be marketed as highly available.

## 6. API gateway architecture

### 6.1 Routes and validation

Canonical client base path is `/api/v1`; the production hostname is not yet verified. The previous `api.hrflow.app` example is illustrative, not evidence of domain ownership. Target route prefixes and ports are defined in the [contract conventions](../REST-API-DATABASE-DESIGN.md). JWT validation checks allowed algorithm RS256, signature, issuer, audience, expiration, not-before, and bounded clock skew. Reject unsigned tokens, algorithm substitution, unknown issuer, and tokens for a different audience. Access tokens contain `sub`, `tenantId`, `employeeId` when linked, `roles`, `iat`, `exp`, and `jti`. Services repeat validation and enforce resource-level rules.

Strip `X-Tenant-Id`, `X-Employee-Id`, and `X-Roles` from public requests. Derive tenant context from the verified token; a tenant switch requires a new token, not a header edit. A login includes tenant slug because email is only unique within a tenant. Public routes are login, refresh, and JWKS; liveness exposure is narrowly configured. Tenant provisioning requires a separate platform credential and is never anonymous. No catch-all route may accidentally expose Actuator, debug, Registry, Kafka UI, or internal jobs.

### 6.2 Proposed edge budgets

| Control | Initial proposal | Validation |
|---|---|---|
| JSON body | 256 KiB except evidence batch capped separately | Over-limit request returns 413 before controller |
| Evidence batch | ≤100 observations and ≤256 KiB | Validate each item, all-or-nothing admission |
| Normal API timeout | 5 seconds | Client timeout greater than edge timeout; preserve idempotency on retry |
| Login limiting | Per tenant/account and source IP; thresholds calibrated | 429 and `Retry-After`; no permanent attacker-triggered lockout |
| SSE | Separate long-lived route; heartbeat every 20 seconds proposed | Proxy idle timeout above heartbeat; per-user connection limit 3 proposed |
| Page size | Default 20, maximum 100 | Reject unsupported sort fields |

These limits are not configured today. The gateway does not automatically retry mutating upstream requests. If the service committed but the connection failed, the client repeats the same key. Return normalized error bodies without exposing upstream stack traces. Preserve a validated UUID correlation ID or generate one; return `X-Correlation-Id`. Do not use the correlation ID as authentication or deduplication identity.

### 6.3 Browser and failure behavior

CORS uses an explicit environment-specific origin allowlist. Cookie-based refresh uses HttpOnly, Secure, appropriate SameSite, origin checks, and CSRF protection. Web access tokens remain in memory; do not place refresh secrets in localStorage. Content security policy, frame restrictions, and output escaping are required for the web deployment. Gateway liveness checks process health; readiness checks ability to route, not every provider's availability. Gateway unavailability yields client network/retry feedback; mobile preserves unsent commands locally. Cached valid keys allow verification during identity downtime until cache/key validity policy expires. Unknown key IDs trigger bounded refresh; fail closed if no valid key can be found.

## 7. Identity, organization, and tenancy

### 7.1 Provisioning and organization

Tenant provisioning creates tenant, first OWNER, and audit event in one identity transaction. Initial credential delivery/activation remains part of O08: use controlled synthetic seed credentials for demos; real owner accounts stay disabled until a reviewed one-time activation process exists. Never email or return a permanent plaintext password. An OWNER may grant HR_ADMIN through a reviewed administration flow; no implicit role inheritance is assumed. Manager hierarchy must be acyclic and within the tenant. Changing a manager emits a revised employee snapshot with effective relationship data. Assignments are effective-dated and non-overlapping for the MVP single-schedule-per-date policy. Site and holiday edits publish snapshots sufficient to update local projections. Department/position display fields needed downstream belong in employee snapshots; consumers do not query identity synchronously.

### 7.2 Passwords and token lifecycle

Proposed authentication ownership is identity-org, consistent with the original API draft. Use a vetted Spring Security password encoder with configurable work factor; never reversible password encryption. Login errors do not reveal whether tenant/email/password was wrong. Access lifetime proposal is ten minutes; refresh lifetime proposal is fourteen days, subject to security review. Store only refresh-token hashes; tokens have high entropy and are opaque. Rotation locks the token family, invalidates the old token, creates one replacement, and commits before response. Reuse of a rotated token revokes the family and requires login; clients serialize refresh attempts. Refresh responses cannot be stored as plaintext idempotency results. Logout revokes the refresh family; access revocation is bounded by short expiration unless a revocation cache is added. Password change revokes other families and records an audit action. Termination/suspension enforcement propagation and the maximum access-token window require explicit launch sign-off.

Publish public signing keys via JWKS only; private keys reside in protected secret storage. Introduce a new key before signing with it; retain old verification keys longer than maximum access lifetime plus skew/cache window. Document emergency key compromise response separately from routine rotation. Gateway and services cache JWKS rather than calling identity per request. No business service receives a reusable tenant administrator token for background jobs.

### 7.3 Tenant isolation layers

| Layer | Required control |
|---|---|
| HTTP | Tenant from verified token; foreign tenant IDs return 404 without existence leakage |
| Queries | Repository predicates require tenant; pagination/counts use the same scope |
| Database | Composite tenant FKs/uniques; distinct service roles; RLS defense-in-depth proposed |
| Events | Producer-owned topic ACL, envelope tenant validation, tenant-scoped references |
| Caches | Key includes tenant, subject/scope, resource and revision |
| Storage | Tenant/resource prefix, authorization before issuing short-lived signed URL |
| Exports | Tenant and requester persisted; reauthorize each status/download request |
| Jobs | Explicit tenant in job record; context reset after each task |
| Logs | No sensitive payload; tenant ID only in access-controlled logs, not high-cardinality metrics |

`search_path` or Hikari schema selection alone does not enforce service ownership. Use runtime roles with grants only on owned schema and a separate migration role. RLS is proposed additional defense; it requires transaction-local tenant setup and pool reset tests before adoption. Even with RLS, application authorization remains required.

# Contracts reference 01

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

- Revision: 2026-10-23; status: planned implementation contract.
- All business endpoints and tables below are **planned**, not implemented controllers or migrations.
- New contract details and explicitly marked extensions are **proposed** pending design review.
- The only implemented HTTP API is the standalone confidence prototype, described separately.
- Related: [architecture](../Architecture.md), [delivery plan](../PLAN.md), [decision records](../Architecture.md).
- Existing endpoint/entity coverage has been retained; malformed tables and ambiguous semantics are replaced here.

## 1. Shared contract conventions

### 1.1 Addressing and identity

Client prefix is `/api/v1`; local target origin is `http://localhost:8080`. No production domain is established. JWKS alone is at root `/.well-known/jwks.json`. Target ports: identity-org 8101, attendance 8102, leave 8103, request 8104, notification 8105, reporting 8106. Attendance currently configures 8082; target routing is not implemented. Identity schema is `identity_org`, matching bootstrap SQL rather than the old draft's `identity` spelling. All prefixes route to the owning service; gateway preserves the public contract while private path rewriting is an implementation choice. Authentication uses bearer JWT validated at gateway and service, except explicit auth/public/control-plane endpoints. Trusted tenant is token `tenantId`, never a client-selected header/body. Roles are EMPLOYEE/MANAGER/HR_ADMIN/OWNER with no automatic role inheritance. `self` requires the token-linked employee; `team` means current direct reports; `participant` means requester or assigned approver. All object queries include tenant and resource scope; cross-tenant/hidden objects return 404. Platform provisioning uses a separate control-plane credential, not a tenant OWNER token.

### 1.2 Data and validation

IDs are UUID strings; UUIDv7 generation is proposed, but validation accepts valid UUID identifiers without assuming sort semantics. JSON is camelCase; SQL is snake_case. Unknown command fields are rejected. Instants are ISO-8601 UTC (`2026-10-22T01:00:00Z`), local dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, local times `HH:mm`, zones IANA strings. Server-generated fields (tenantId, actor, status transitions, balances, revision) are never mass assigned. Strings default to trimmed non-empty ≤255 characters; reason/comment ≤2000; email ≤254 and normalized for uniqueness. Pagination: `page` ≥0, `size` 1–100 (default 20), allowlisted `sort` (default createdAt desc, ID tiebreaker). Date ranges default to current work date/month as endpoint indicates, maximum 366 days proposed; exports may use separately approved limits. List response: `{items, page, size, total}`; projected responses additionally contain `asOf`, `projectionLagMs`, `isStale`. GET is side-effect free, except access audit logging; lists never bypass scope for total counts.

### 1.3 Headers and concurrency

All protected routes: `Authorization: Bearer <access-token>`. Optional validated UUID `X-Correlation-Id` is echoed/generated; client identity headers are stripped. POST commands require `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` unless explicitly exempt below. Scope key by tenant, actor, method, canonical path; store canonical body hash and committed response in the same transaction. Same key/body returns original status/body/Location; different body returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH. Concurrent duplicates serialize at a unique constraint; an in-flight operation may return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After if lock wait exceeds budget. Only committed success is cached; validation/transient failures can retry safely. Proposed retention is ≥30 days; mobile automatic retry horizon ≤7 days, after which user reconciliation is required. Mutable resources expose `version` and ETag `"<version>"`; PATCH/PUT/DELETE and decision commands require `If-Match` unless explicitly exempt. Missing If-Match is 428; mismatched version is 412. State conflicts are 409, business policy violations 422. Create commands use row locks/uniques to handle concurrent creation even without an existing version.

### 1.4 HTTP and errors

201 = created and durably committed, with Location; 200 = read or completed transition; 204 = completed deletion/revocation without body. 202 = durable background job accepted with status URL; not every event-producing write is asynchronous HTTP. 400 = invalid syntax/field shape; 401 = authentication failure; 403 = visible but unauthorized operation; 404 = absent/hidden object. 409 = state/idempotency/concurrency conflict; 412 = stale precondition; 413 = body too large; 422 = business rule; 428 = missing precondition. 429 includes Retry-After; 503 indicates transient unavailability/reference freshness failure when retry is appropriate. No stack traces, tokens, private location, or object keys appear in error messages.

```json
{
  "code": "LEAVE_BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT",
  "message": "Insufficient available leave.",
  "details": [
    {
      "field": "endDate",
      "issue": "Requested units exceed availability."
    }
  ],
  "traceId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000040"
}
```


For every protected endpoint, common errors are 400/401/403/404/429/503; mutating operations add 409/422 and precondition errors where applicable. Read retries are safe; command retries preserve key/body/version. A timeout after commit must be reconciled by key, not a new submission. Normal transaction boundary is one owner-service DB transaction including audit, idempotency result, and outbox for listed business events. No cross-service transaction is implied. GET observes owner state or a freshness-labeled local projection.

All relative paths in entries are shown as full public paths. Every endpoint is planned. The preserved catalog is extended only where a necessary workflow/status/security gap is identified explicitly.

### API-001: POST /api/v1/auth/login

- Owner: `identity-org`; status: planned.
- Purpose and validation: Authenticate within tenant; generic invalid-credential error; no account enumeration.
- Authorization and tenant scope: public; tenantSlug required; shared token/tenant/object rules apply.
- Profile: AUTH; shared headers, errors, transaction, pagination and retry behavior from section 2.2 apply.
- Parameters: no path parameters; no query parameters.
- Request schema: Login; response schema: Tokens.
- Success: 200; explicit overrides in purpose take precedence. Errors: shared profile codes; endpoint validation yields 422 and state conflict 409.
- Side effects/events: no Kafka business event; local mutation/audit only for command profiles.
- Request example: `{"tenantSlug":"demo","email":"employee@example.test","password":"example-only-secret"}`

# Contracts reference 15

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## Continued reference

### reporting.auditlog

Owner: `reporting` service schema. Purpose: Owner-local append-only audit; opaque actor IDs are not cross-service FK.

Retention: AUDIT; immutable fact/action; insert-only normal role.

PK and all FK/unique/check constraints are declared below; listed indexes serve tenant-scoped lookups/queues. If no extra index is listed, the primary/unique index serves the expected access path.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "reporting"."audit_log" (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  id uuid NOT NULL,
  actor_id uuid,
  action text NOT NULL,
  entity text NOT NULL,
  entity_id uuid,
  diff jsonb NOT NULL,
  at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  correlation_id uuid NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,id)
);
CREATE INDEX "reporting_audit_log_q1" ON "reporting"."audit_log" (tenant_id,at,id);
```


### reporting.inbox

Owner: `reporting` service schema. Purpose: Deduplication record committed with local effect, before Kafka offset acknowledgment.

Retention: TRANSIT; immutable fact/action; insert-only normal role.

PK and all FK/unique/check constraints are declared below; listed indexes serve tenant-scoped lookups/queues. If no extra index is listed, the primary/unique index serves the expected access path.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "reporting"."inbox" (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  consumer_name text NOT NULL,
  event_id uuid NOT NULL,
  topic text NOT NULL,
  partition integer NOT NULL,
  source_offset bigint NOT NULL,
  aggregate_id text NOT NULL,
  aggregate_version bigint NOT NULL,
  processed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,consumer_name,event_id)
);
```


### reporting.idempotencyrecord

Owner: `reporting` service schema. Purpose: Committed safe HTTP result; do not persist login/refresh token responses.

Retention: TRANSIT; immutable fact/action; insert-only normal role.

PK and all FK/unique/check constraints are declared below; listed indexes serve tenant-scoped lookups/queues. If no extra index is listed, the primary/unique index serves the expected access path.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "reporting"."idempotency_record" (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  command_scope text NOT NULL,
  idempotency_key uuid NOT NULL,
  request_hash char(64) NOT NULL,
  response_status integer NOT NULL CHECK (response_status BETWEEN 200 AND 299),
  response_body jsonb,
  resource_id uuid,
  location text,
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,command_scope,idempotency_key)
);
CREATE INDEX "reporting_idempotency_record_q1" ON "reporting"."idempotency_record" (expires_at);
```


### 4.4 Integrity, concurrency, and migration review

The DDL enforces tenant-scoped uniqueness, same-service composite FKs, open-session uniqueness, nonnegative balances, and inbox IDs. It intentionally does not claim every domain invariant is expressible with a row check:

- Employee_shift date-range overlap needs employee-row serialization or a reviewed exclusion constraint migration; the unique start date is insufficient alone.
- Closed session overlap needs employee/day guard plus interval validation under lock.
- Leave FULL versus AM/PM overlap needs employee guard and active-request/day lookup; historical day rows remain after cancellation.
- Request approver != requester spans two rows and must be checked inside the request lock transaction.
- Tenant/employee consistency of leave_request_day is enforced by the additional composite parent constraint in section 4.5.
- Refresh family rotation and token reuse detection need a family/user lock and retained revocation history.
- Device token reassignment must atomically deactivate prior ownership; do not let nullable uniqueness or provider duplicates leak notifications.
- Delivery target_id is made non-null in section 4.5; email/in-app uses stable logical recipient IDs.
- Notification preference-set ETag uses preference_set (section 4.5); lock it while replacing category rows.
- Batch read-all captures one cutoff in the idempotency transaction.

All services use bounded row locks, deterministic lock ordering, and retry-safe commands. No balance mutation is a read-modify-write without a lock/version predicate. Current session checkout may update the session projection, but evidence/correction_action/audit/ledger remain append-only. Apply initial schemas/tables through owner Flyway migrations; this Markdown DDL is not already installed. Before launch, test migration order, runtime grants, query plans, upgrade compatibility, rollback, retention cleanup, and tenant-predicate enforcement. Do not partition evidence until volume warrants it and uniqueness across partitions is deliberately redesigned. Projection rebuilds run in isolated tables/consumer groups, with external side effects disabled.

### 4.5 Supporting aggregate guards and integrity extensions

These proposed tables/constraints complete the aggregate behaviors that cannot rely on individual row versions alone.

### notification.preferenceset

Owner: notification. Purpose: one lock/version for the entire own preference resource; tenant-scoped employee FK. Retention MASTER; audited mutable state. GET/PUT ETag uses this version, not per-category row versions. No extra index beyond PK is needed.

```sql
CREATE TABLE notification.preference_set (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  employee_id uuid NOT NULL,
  locale text NOT NULL CHECK (locale IN ('en','km')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,employee_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id,employee_id) REFERENCES notification.employee_ref(tenant_id,employee_id)
);
ALTER TABLE notification.notification_pref DROP COLUMN locale;
ALTER TABLE notification.delivery_attempt ALTER COLUMN target_id SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE leave.leave_request ADD CONSTRAINT leave_request_employee_identity UNIQUE (tenant_id,id,
  employee_id);
ALTER TABLE leave.leave_request_day ADD CONSTRAINT leave_day_parent_employee_fk
  FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id,request_id,employee_id) REFERENCES leave.leave_request(tenant_id,id,
  employee_id);
ALTER TABLE attendance.cutoff_job ADD COLUMN kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('CHECK_IN',
  'CHECK_OUT'));
ALTER TABLE attendance.cutoff_job DROP CONSTRAINT
  cutoff_job_tenant_id_employee_id_work_date_shift_revision_key;
ALTER TABLE attendance.cutoff_job ADD CONSTRAINT cutoff_business_key UNIQUE (tenant_id,employee_id,
  work_date,shift_revision,kind);
```


Cutoff kind distinguishes initial absence assessment from missing-checkout finalization on the same shift revision. Delivery target_id is a stable non-null logical recipient/device target, even for email or in-app channel; this makes attempt uniqueness effective. Leave day employee identity is now enforced by a composite parent FK as well as owner transaction checks. Identity tables without a transitive tenant reference also reference the root directly:

```sql
ALTER TABLE identity_org.department ADD FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES identity_org.tenant(id);
ALTER TABLE identity_org.position ADD FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES identity_org.tenant(id);
ALTER TABLE identity_org.work_site ADD FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES identity_org.tenant(id);
ALTER TABLE identity_org.holiday ADD FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES identity_org.tenant(id);
```


Runtime grants must restrict inserts into all owner schemas to authorized tenant context. Root FKs are integrity, not authorization. Each supporting table follows the common migration/version/retention rules; these are documentation examples, not applied repository migrations.

# Plan reference 01

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## 1. Purpose and baseline

Revision: 2026-10-23. Status: implementation plan, not a completion report. HRFlow is a placeholder product name for an event-driven multi-tenant HR platform. The twelve-week clock starts at an agreed kickoff; no calendar start date or historical completion is assumed. Contributor A owns backend, web, infrastructure, and operations preparation; contributor B owns Flutter and mobile validation. A tenant/product representative must decide HR policy; neither developer silently decides legal retention or leave precedence.

Source of truth: [architecture](../Architecture.md) for boundaries/behavior, [API/database/event specification](../REST-API-DATABASE-DESIGN.md) for contracts, this document for sequence and acceptance. [Requirement IDs R01–R12](../Architecture.md) connect work to tests. [Open questions O01–O08](../Architecture.md) are explicit decision gates.

Current evidence: seven Java startup scaffolds, two partial shared libraries, Nuxt welcome page, local dependency Compose, and a standalone confidence prototype. There are no implemented business REST controllers, migrations, outbox/inbox workers, Flutter source here, CI workflows, or cloud deployment resources. The existing five Python tests and starter web build are useful but do not demonstrate HRFlow end to end. The earlier plan's week-12 vision service and Avro migration are not mandatory delivery: vision is unapproved optional scope, and serialization must be decided early rather than migrated during final hardening.

## 2. Goals, scope, and release tiers

Goal: demonstrate a reliable authenticated check-in, auditable leave/request approvals, and tenant-safe visibility, with recoverable asynchronous delivery. The smallest valuable slice is login → schedule projection → durable check-in → notification/report projection → visible client result. No payroll, recruitment, continuous GPS, biometric-template collection, or authoritative inventory management is included.

| Tier | Included capabilities | Exit standard |
|---|---|---|
| MVP | Auth/RBAC/tenant/resource checks; employee/shift/holiday setup; check-in/out and statuses; leave balances/approval; material and special requests; inbox and one push path; audit/corrections; CSV reports; reproducible deployment | R01–R10 tested end to end |
| Should-have | Geofence/Wi-Fi reminders; rule-based inference and next-day confirmation; SSE live view; EN/KH; XLSX | Only after correctness/recovery gates pass |
| Stretch | ML confidence integration, NFC, dark mode | Separate evidence and explicit capacity approval |
| Production launch | Secrets/TLS/grants; reviewed policies; monitoring; restore/rollback; security review and operator | Required before real users, even if demo MVP is complete |
| Future optional | Vision/camera processing, complex inventory, service extraction/scaling, EKS | Separate ADR and schedule |

Inference target ≥90% recovery ±10 minutes and battery target <3% remain pilot research targets, not MVP release promises. Do not spend the core platform schedule improving synthetic ML metrics.

## 3. Responsibilities and working agreements

| Responsibility | A | B | External decision owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Domain/API/event/database design | Author and implement | Review client needs and fixtures | HR/product approves business ambiguity |
| Backend and shared event foundation | Primary | Test client retry/error behavior | Security reviewer for auth/isolation |
| Web | Primary; narrow screens first | Cross-check mobile parity | HR representative usability |
| Flutter/offline/device/push | Supply contracts and test environment | Primary | Device/platform account owner |
| Infrastructure/CI/restore | Primary | Smoke test release on devices | Operator/budget owner |
| Acceptance/demo | Joint | Joint | Product signs evidence, not undocumented claims |

A's backend/web/infra work is sequentially prioritized within each week, not three simultaneous full-time workstreams. B uses agreed JSON fixtures and mocks until the first slice is live. Contract changes require both contributors' review and updated examples/tests before implementation diverges. Daily integration uses synthetic tenant fixtures; weekly exit review records passing evidence and remaining blockers. No percentage-complete claims based on directories or dependencies alone.

## 4. Dependencies and work breakdown

| Work package | Prerequisites | Output | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| WP1 foundation | Repository access, Java 21, Docker | Working toolchain/config, version/serialization/client decisions | R10 |
| WP2 contracts and mocks | O01/O06, policy assumptions | Auth/attendance API fixtures, event envelope, error model | R01–R04 |
| WP3 identity/security | WP1/WP2 | Tenant/user/employee/shift/holiday, JWT/refresh, grants | R01/R02 |
| WP4 reliability | WP1/WP2 | Migrations, outbox/inbox, compatibility/retry/replay tests | R04 |
| WP5 attendance slice | WP3/WP4 | Idempotent check-in/out, projection, minimal client views | R03/R07 |
| WP6 leave | Stable org snapshots, O02 | Locked reservations/ledger, approvals/conflicts | R05 |
| WP7 requests | Org/roles, WP4 | Advisory material forms and assigned chain | R06 |
| WP8 reporting/audit | Stable daily/leave/request facts | Corrections, authorized CSV, shadow rebuild | R08/R09 |
| WP9 delivery/operations | Reproducible build, O04/O05/O08 | Staging/pilot deploy, smoke, rollback, restore | R10 |
| WP10 hardening | WP5–WP9 | Failure/security/load/device evidence and demo | R01–R12 |

No feature team can assume a projection is populated merely because Kafka is running. Seed identity data through the owner API/migrations and verify downstream revisions before attendance acceptance.

## 5. Twelve-week roadmap

Each weekly gate is an exit condition, not a date-driven permission to move broken foundations forward. If a gate fails, use section 10 cut lines and explicitly revise scope; do not skip security/durability.

### Week 1 — Reproducible foundation and first contracts

- Owner: A primary; B reviews contract/client requirements.
- Dependencies: repository/tools; external O01 web choice, O06 serialization choice, O07 Maven policy.
- A sequence: correct documented startup/config defects; establish Java 21 build; choose inheritance without unnecessary upgrades; create first migrations/contracts and local launch instructions.
- B sequence: confirm Flutter repository/toolchain; create auth/home feature skeleton and mock API client.
- Deliverables: auth/check-in/today JSON schemas/examples, error/idempotency conventions, synthetic two-tenant fixtures, build/config checks, decision notes.
- Tests: clean dependency startup; schema generation; gateway route smoke; mock contract/example validation; full Java compile under target JDK.
- Acceptance/exit: fresh checkout can build the first modules, PostgreSQL initializes intended schemas, Registry connects if selected, and B can exercise mock success/error/retry shapes.
- Risks: existing wrong Compose mount/Registry listener, malformed YAML, Avro path, mixed parents; unresolved external Flutter location.

### Week 2 — Identity and reliability infrastructure

- Owner: A backend/foundation; B mobile auth.
- Dependencies: week 1; O08 authentication policy; O03 initial date/correction constraints.
- A sequence: implement login/refresh/logout, trusted tenant context and service authorization; then outbox/inbox and local integration harness.
- B: secure token storage, serialized refresh, logout, authentication errors; role-appropriate shell.
- Deliverables: synthetic tenant/user provisioning, employee seed path, rotating tokens, starter auto-configuration and migrations, durable relay/consumer example.
- Tests: forged headers/JWT, tenant ID substitution, refresh reuse, unique inbox, crash after broker ack, offset-after-commit behavior.
- Acceptance/exit: one employee can log in and refresh; wrong tenant cannot read data; business write survives relay crash without repeated effect.
- Risks: overbuilding identity UX; narrow admin provisioning before broad user management.

### Week 3 — Organization projections and first check-in

- Owner: A backend then minimal admin web; B profile/home/check-in client.
- Dependencies: week 2; stable employee/shift/holiday snapshots and topic keys.
- A sequence: owner CRUD for employee/site/shift/assignment/holiday, snapshot consumers, employee/day guard, idempotent check-in.
- B: real login/profile integration, stable key persisted before sending, check-in UI with clear pending state.
- Deliverables: active schedule visible to attendance, source revisions, 201 session response, outbox fact, minimal Nuxt-or-approved web setup form.
- Tests: missing projection, duplicate key/body, changed body/same key, parallel same-employee check-in, effective dates and tenant constraints.
- Acceptance/exit: phone/mocked mobile checks in once with one evidence/session/outbox effect; API can query today after timeout retry.
- Risks: reference ordering and stale assignment data; fail explicitly rather than guessing shift.

### Week 4 — Checkout and visible end-to-end result

- Owner: A attendance and minimal notification/report projection; B checkout/offline queue.
- Dependencies: week 3; working event foundation.
- A: implement checkout, day calculations and flags, minimal inbox plus daily projection, narrow dashboard view.
- B: local durable queue, network-loss recovery, checkout If-Match handling, current state screen, local biometric unlock if feasible.
- Deliverables: full first vertical slice, freshness-labeled daily state, deterministic shift/date fixtures.
- Tests: checkout before check-in; stale version; duplicate checkout; offline retry after commit; two closed sessions and one-open constraint.
- Acceptance/exit: check-in/out appears on phone and authorized web view; restart does not lose commands; no model/provider call on hot path.
- Risks: expanding all notification channels early; implement durable inbox before providers.

### Week 5 — MVP-1 and deployment rehearsal

- Owner: A CI/deploy then notification provider; B device registration/push validation.
- Dependencies: week 4; O04 hosting budget decision; provider development credentials.
- A: establish PR checks/image build, first staging/container deployment, secret handling, inbox-to-push worker and backlog metrics.
- B: register/deactivate push tokens; receive generic notification; validate permission refusal and foreground/background behavior.
- Deliverables: reproducible staged attendance demo, operational signal dashboard/log queries, kill-consumer evidence, provider acceptance state.
- Tests: stop notification/check in/restart; one logical notification; provider timeout/invalid token; deploy smoke and basic rollback.
- Acceptance/exit: MVP-1 proves durable attendance independently of consumer/provider availability; B uses staged API rather than only local mocks.
- Risks: deployment/provider account delays; preserve inbox and local test environment while escalating dependency, do not claim push delivery without device evidence.

### Week 6 — Leave submission and balance safety

- Owner: A leave domain; B leave forms/history.
- Dependencies: org projections, outbox/inbox; O02 leave/calendar conflict policy reviewed.
- A: type/policy setup, day expansion, balance/ledger, pending reservation, self-service leave endpoints.
- B: type/balance loading, date/half-day validation, stable command keys, own request history.
- Deliverables: authoritative balances, policy snapshot and expanded days, private attachment path where required.
- Tests: simultaneous requests, insufficient balance, AM/PM/FULL overlap, holidays excluded, year boundary locks, duplicate submission.
- Acceptance/exit: two parallel requests cannot overspend; available balance and ledger agree; mobile shows authoritative response/failure.
- Risks: complex accrual; start with configured upfront entitlement, retain monthly/year-end as gated admin capabilities.

### Week 7 — Leave approval and conflict recovery

- Owner: A saga/manager web; B approval and cancellation screens.
- Dependencies: week 6; approved O02 conflict semantics, assigned approver scope.
- A: approve/reject/cancel, attendance leave overlays, conflict detection, NEEDS_REVIEW handling and resolution; balance report event.
- B: manager actions with If-Match, stale-state reload, cancellation and visible syncState.
- Deliverables: leave end-to-end, revised day status, conflict inbox, compensating ledger path and reconciliation procedure.
- Tests: self-approval denied, duplicate approval once, cancel-before-delayed-approval, conflict-after-cancel ignored, stopped attendance then replay.
- Acceptance/exit: approved leave reaches attendance eventually; cancellation reverses exactly once; unresolved conflicts never silently overwrite manual work.
- Risks: saga complexity; keep one approver and full-day baseline before extra policy variants.

### Week 8 — Requests and MVP-2

- Owner: A request service and narrow HR catalogue/approval view; B request forms/inbox.
- Dependencies: org/roles, typed form contracts, attachment quarantine path.
- A: draft/submit, advisory material lines, snapshotted one-or-two-step approvals, rejection/cancel/fulfill and workflow events.
- B: dynamic bounded form, draft recovery, participant comments, assigned approval screens.
- Deliverables: materials/general requests, actor audit, validated uploads/downloads, final decision notifications.
- Tests: concurrent step decisions, unauthorized approver, self approval, draft-only edit, cross-tenant attachment, duplicate fulfillment.
- Acceptance/exit: MVP-2 demonstrates attendance, leave, and material request with secure approval and asynchronous visibility.
- Risks: inventory creep; stock remains advisory; no purchasing/warehouse subsystem.

### Week 9 — Corrections, audit, and reports

- Owner: A corrections/reporting then export web; B correction flows.
- Dependencies: stable event revisions; decision windows O03.
- A: correction/action ledger, manual replacement revision, authorized summary projections, CSV jobs, projection freshness/rebuild.
- B: correction submit/review result, original-versus-effective history, report summary if needed.
- Deliverables: auditable timesheet correction, tenant-scoped dashboard/calendar/CSV, job polling and expiring download.
- Tests: raw evidence unchanged, double approval race, out-of-order daily snapshot, summary subtract/add, formula-safe CSV, revoked role before download, shadow rebuild counts.
- Acceptance/exit: corrected day produces a higher revision and one accurate export; projection rebuild creates no real notifications.
- Risks: reporting UI expansion; deliver specified CSV before XLSX/charts.

### Week 10 — Cutoff, operations, and should-have gate

- Owner: A cutoff/security/operations; B reminder/device validation.
- Dependencies: all core flows and stable staging; O05 privacy/retention reviewed before evidence collection.
- A: durable absent cutoff, missing-checkout handling, restore/rollback rehearsal, runbooks; add rule inference only if core gates pass.
- B: permission-aware nudges, battery/background tests, inferred confirmation if enabled; EN/KH if capacity remains.
- Deliverables: restart-safe cutoff, reviewed operational controls, optional rules path with explicit pending state.
- Tests: holiday/leave/stale-projection cutoff, repeated job, late evidence after finalization, consent denied, no continuous GPS, backup restore.
- Acceptance/exit: absence is not inferred from missing projections; restored system passes tenant/ledger/outbox checks; optional inference can be disabled without breaking attendance.
- Risks: overcommitting geofence/ML or Kubernetes; cut those before resilience/security work.

### Week 11 — Hardening and conditional pilot

- Owner: A load/security/recovery, B device/offline acceptance, product/HR policy sign-off.
- Dependencies: week 10 release controls; approved real-data policy and operator.
- A: execute 100-concurrent scenario, p95/p99/error/propagation measurement, authorization review, migration upgrade rehearsal.
- B: representative Android/iOS device tests, token expiry/rotation, offline/conflicting commands, accessibility/localization checks.
- Deliverables: test evidence, known limitations, release candidate, pilot feedback for 5–10 consenting users if launch gate passes.
- Tests: two-tenant adversarial matrix, kill relay/consumer, broker outage, export isolation, smoke/rollback and restore.
- Acceptance/exit: no unresolved critical isolation/durability defect; measured targets either pass or have explicit scoped remediation; pilot is blocked if real-data controls are unapproved.
- Risks: pilot feedback consumes feature time; prioritize defects and keep feature freeze.

### Week 12 — Freeze, release decision, and demonstration

- Owner: A+B; product/operator approve release evidence.
- Dependencies: week 11; no new feature work unless required to fix a blocking defect.
- A: repair verified blockers, finalize deployment/runbooks/contract traceability and reproducibility; record immutable release artifacts.
- B: final device smoke, user guide/demo recording, confirm queued-command recovery on release candidate.
- Deliverables: demonstrable build, release notes, measured test report, open-risk register, operational handover and demo video.
- Tests: exact release-image smoke, end-to-end attendance/leave/request/correction/export, consumer restart, authorized access and rollback verification.
- Acceptance/exit: all MVP definition-of-done evidence linked, demo reproducible, limitations disclosed; production launch can remain blocked even when synthetic demo is complete.
- Risks: last-minute framework/cloud/schema changes; defer to next increment rather than destabilize release.

## 6. Integration milestones

| Milestone | Owner | Dependencies | Deliverable / verifiable exit | Required tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 end W1 | A+B | Toolchain, O01/O06/O07 | Mockable auth/check-in/today and clean setup | Compile, schema/examples, dependency health |
| M1 end W2 | A | M0, O08 | Tenant-auth and durable event foundation | JWT/header/tenant, relay crash/inbox |
| M2 end W4 | A+B | M1 + org | First phone-to-dashboard slice | Keys, checkout, offline retry, projection |
| MVP-1 end W5 | A+B | M2 + staging | Durable attendance and notification recovery | Kill consumer, provider failure, deploy smoke |
| M3 end W7 | A+B | Leave balances + O02 | Approval/cancel/conflict end to end | Reservation race, stale conflict, compensation |
| MVP-2 end W8 | A+B | M3 + request chain | Material/general requests end to end | Approval race, attachment isolation |
| RC end W10 | A+B | Audit/reports/ops | Core complete, cutoff and recoverability | Rebuild/export, restore, cutoff |
| Release end W12 | A+B+product/operator | Security/policy gates | Reproducible release or explicitly limited demo | Final E2E/load/device/rollback evidence |

A missed milestone is recorded with blocker, owner, revised dependency, and scope impact; later milestone labels are not claimed complete automatically.

## 7. Quality gates and definition of done

A feature is done only when:

1. Contract, authorization, tenant scope, validation, error and retry semantics are reviewed.
1. Owner migration/constraints/indexes and current-state/append-only behavior are tested on PostgreSQL.
1. Mutation, audit, idempotency, and outbox share one transaction where required.
1. Consumer transaction/inbox and offset behavior are tested for duplicates and out-of-order data.
1. The client handles loading/empty/error/stale/offline states without duplicating commands.
1. Acceptance tests cover the requirement ID and negative role/tenant cases.
1. Logging/metrics reveal failure without exposing secrets or unnecessary personal data.
1. Documentation and machine contracts reflect actual implementation status.
1. Clean build and release smoke pass; remaining limitations are disclosed.

No fixed test coverage percentage is required or claimed. Test depth follows failure risk, not line count. Business unit tests do not replace PostgreSQL/Kafka integration tests for durability and locking.

## 8. Release readiness

### Synthetic demonstration gate

- [ ] Two synthetic tenants and employees can be provisioned reproducibly.
- [ ] Login/check-in/out, leave, request, correction, and CSV flows work on release candidate.
- [ ] Duplicate keys and consumer restart produce one business effect.
- [ ] Freshness and asynchronous job status are visible.
- [ ] Exact toolchain/configuration and startup order are documented.
- [ ] No production credentials or real evidence are needed for demo.

### Real-user launch gate

- [ ] O02/O03/O05/O08 policies approved or dependent feature disabled explicitly.
- [ ] TLS, key rotation, refresh revocation window, runtime/migration grants reviewed.
- [ ] Resource-level and cross-tenant tests pass for APIs/SSE/files/exports/jobs.
- [ ] Attachment privacy/quarantine, evidence minimization, retention/erasure process verified.
- [ ] Deployment target, cost forecast, operator/backup, monitoring and incident contacts agreed.
- [ ] Backup restore and compatible rollback demonstrated; RPO/RTO agreed from evidence.
- [ ] No open critical security/data-loss defects; known lower risks accepted with owner/date.
- [ ] Real-device permissions/offline/push behavior and employee consent verified.

These boxes are acceptance criteria, not a claim that any check has already passed.

## 9. Risk register and assumptions

| Risk | Likelihood / impact | Mitigation | Owner / trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| A overloaded across seven services/web/infra | High / high | Narrow slice, sequential work, merge projections if needed | A; missed weekly gate |
| B blocked by unstable APIs | High / high | W1 fixtures/mocks and contract review before changes | A+B; payload drift |
| Tenant leakage | Medium / critical | Scoped query/constraint/event/file test matrix; block launch | A/security; any isolation failure |
| Event duplicate/order defect | High / high | Outbox/inbox plus aggregate revisions, crash/replay tests | A; repeated/wrong effects |
| Attendance precedence ambiguity | High / high | O02 decision and visible review state | Product/HR; before W7 |
| Policy/timezone complexity | Medium / high | Same-day MVP, explicit snapshots, reject unsupported cases | A/HR; W2 |
| Cloud budget/cluster overhead | High / high | Cost forecast, simple pilot target, no EKS mandate | A/operator; W5 |
| Device/background delivery limits | High / medium | Explicit check-in fallback; real-device evidence | B; W5/W10 |
| Synthetic ML confidence mistaken for accuracy | Medium / high | Defer ML; separate real labeled test set | A/product; any auto-inference proposal |
| Provider/account unavailable | Medium / medium | Durable inbox and clear pending state; resolve account dependency | A+B; W5 |
| Registry/build/config scaffold defects | High / high | W1 repair and full compile/startup gates | A; M0 |
| Privacy/retention approval absent | Medium / critical | Synthetic data only until approved | Tenant/security; before pilot |
| Scope creep to inventory/vision/payroll | Medium / high | Explicit change gate and cut line | Product; new request |

Assumptions: contributors are available for the full twelve-week effort; HR/product can decide policies promptly; test devices and provider accounts are available; repository contains all current backend/web source. Flutter repository, production domain, hosting budget, legal policy, and availability commitment are unknown until confirmed.

## 10. Scope changes and contingency

Any change records business value, affected requirement/contract, effort, risk, owner, and displaced work. A+B review API/event implications; product/HR approves business-policy changes; operator approves hosting changes. Do not add scope by silently redefining “enterprise-grade” to require more infrastructure.

Cut first: ML, vision, NFC, dark mode, distributed tracing, Kafka Streams, Redis, DLQ UI, advanced inference, XLSX, custom charts, Kubernetes/EKS. Next simplify: keep one push provider, narrow approval chains, merge reporting/notification projections, seed low-frequency admin data through controlled tools. EN/KH and reminders remain should-have and can be deferred with explicit product notice. Never cut: authentication/tenant isolation, resource authorization, durable attendance, leave and general requests, outbox/inbox, audit/corrections, tested deployment/recovery. Do not remove policy checks or downgrade deduplication to meet the latency target. If core scope exceeds twelve weeks, present a demonstrable synthetic MVP and a revised production backlog rather than claim launch readiness.

## 11. Demonstration sequence

1. Provision company, employee, assignment, and holiday; show two-tenant isolation.
1. Log in on mobile; check in and show committed response plus dashboard freshness.
1. Repeat the same command/key; show unchanged session/event count.
1. Stop notification consumer, check in with another employee, restart; show one recovered notification.
1. Approve leave; show eventual calendar update, then conflict/cancel recovery with ledger evidence.
1. Submit/approve/fulfill material request; show assigned-approver authorization.
1. Correct a time record; show original evidence and new effective revision.
1. Export authorized CSV; show job status and expired/revoked download behavior.
1. If enabled, demonstrate consent-based nudge/inferred confirmation with uncertainty disclosed.
1. Show measured 100-client results, reproducible deployment, CI evidence, rollback/restore and open limitations.

Kubernetes pods/Terraform are shown only if actually implemented; they are not required props for a successful product demo.

## 12. Requirements-to-test traceability

| Requirement | Delivery gate | Test artifact required |
|---|---|---|
| R01 auth/tenant | W2 then every feature | JWT/refresh/header and tenant/object matrix |
| R02 org/calendar | W3 | Assignment/holiday/source-version fixtures |
| R03 check-in/out | W4 | Atomic transaction, duplicate/parallel/offline cases |
| R04 event recovery | W2/W5/W11 | Relay crash, inbox/order/kill-consumer evidence |
| R05 leave | W6–W7 | Balance lock, reservation, overlap, saga/cancel tests |
| R06 requests | W8 | Chain, self-approval, file access, fulfillment races |
| R07 notification/live | W5/W9 | Logical dedupe, provider acceptance, SSE reconnect/freshness |
| R08 audit/correction | W9 | Immutable evidence/actions, approved replacement revision |
| R09 reporting | W9 | Revision guard, rebuild counts, authorized CSV/job expiry |
| R10 deployment/ops | W1/W5/W10/W12 | Fresh setup, image smoke, rollback/restore report |
| R11 evidence/inference | Conditional W10–W11 | Consent/device/battery and independent labeled evaluation |
| R12 performance | W11 | Hardware/dataset/config, p95/p99/error/propagation samples |

Current passing checks are documented in the validation record, not treated as satisfaction of these future feature gates.
