# Analysis reference 01

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

Reviewed: 22 October 2026. Scope: current working tree, including staged, modified, and untracked source files. This is a code and documentation assessment, not a production runtime audit. Existing application code was not changed.

> **Note:** Historical reconnaissance snapshot: the documentation suite was subsequently expanded. Empty-document and React-plan observations below describe the earlier review state, not the revised specification. See [current architecture](../Architecture.md).

## 1. Overall assessment

HRFlow has a detailed product and architecture plan, an initial Java multi-service skeleton, local infrastructure definitions, a default Nuxt application, and a standalone Python attendance-confidence prototype. It does not yet implement an end-to-end HR workflow.

The largest gap is between the architecture described in `docs/Plan.md` and the executable backend. All seven Java services contain only their Spring Boot entry-point class. There are no business controllers, entities, repositories, migrations, Kafka listeners, authentication flows, or domain services. The shared event starter has dependencies and configuration but no implementation. The Python service is substantially further developed than the core HR platform.

The next milestone should be one authenticated, tenant-isolated attendance flow with persistent data, transactional event publication, and a visible web result. Developing all seven services in parallel would multiply integration work before proving the central workflow.

## 2. Repository structure and ownership

```text
hrflow/
  pom.xml                         Maven aggregator and parent for libraries
  services/
    api-gateway/                  Spring Cloud Gateway MVC dependency; entry point
    identity-org/                 Entry point and generated dependency setup
    attendance/                   Entry point plus PostgreSQL/Kafka configuration
    leave/                        Entry point and generated dependency setup
    request/                      Entry point and generated dependency setup
    notification/                 Entry point and generated dependency setup
    reporting/                    Entry point and generated dependency setup
  libs/
    hrflow-contracts/             One Avro schema and generation configuration
    hrflow-event-starter/         Dependencies and Kafka YAML; no Java source
  web/                            Nuxt/Vue starter
  ml/confidence-service/           FastAPI scoring API, rules, training, tests, model
  infra/
    docker/                       PostgreSQL, Kafka, UI, Schema Registry
    scripts/                      Topic creation script
  docs/                           Detailed plan plus empty design placeholders
  .github/workflows/              Empty
```


This structure expresses intended ownership clearly. However, directory boundaries alone do not establish service isolation. There are no database roles, application contracts, or domain implementations enforcing those boundaries yet. Flutter source, Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflows are absent.

## 3. Product model and intended workflows

The plan describes a multi-tenant HR platform centered on attendance, with organization data, leave approval, material/special requests, notifications, and reports. Payroll and recruitment are explicitly outside scope.

The planned check-in flow is well oriented toward low latency: attendance reads local employee and shift projections, writes evidence, session, and outbox rows in one database transaction, then returns without waiting for downstream services. Notification and reporting consume published events later. This avoids making user success depend on notification availability.

The leave workflow is a choreographed saga: approved leave reaches attendance; attendance detects conflicts; leave moves a conflicted request to review. This requires explicit transition rules, event ordering, duplicate handling, and reconciliation. None is implemented yet.

The plan's attendance precedence is holiday, approved leave, manual, inferred, absent. This needs clarification: approved leave overriding a manual check-in must be reconciled with the separate statement that manual records always win. Preserve raw evidence independently of the calculated daily status so corrections and conflicts remain auditable.

Other unresolved domain decisions include overnight shifts, employee/site time zones, daylight-saving boundaries, multiple sessions in a day, shift reassignment effective dates, partial-day leave, and whether a correction recalculates historical reports. `workDate` must have a defined relationship to shift-local dates rather than server calendar dates.

## 4. Implementation compared with the plan

| Area | Planned | Present in source |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Tenants, JWT, RBAC, employees, shifts, holidays | Application entry point and dependencies |
| Gateway | Routing, authentication, tenant context, rate limiting | MVC gateway dependency; no routes or security policy |
| Attendance | Check-in/out, status, evidence, corrections, inference | Entry point and datasource/Kafka configuration |
| Leave and requests | Balances, approval workflows, conflict handling | Entry points and dependencies |
| Notification | Push/email, in-app inbox, SSE | Entry point and dependencies |
| Reporting | Projections, dashboards, CSV | Entry point and dependencies |
| Event foundation | Outbox, inbox, retries, DLQ, correlation | Library skeleton and one Avro schema |
| Web | React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, feature screens | Nuxt/Vue welcome screen |
| Mobile | Flutter, biometrics, offline queue | No mobile source in this repository |
| ML | Stretch feature, evidence confidence | Functional standalone prototype with five passing tests |
| Delivery | CI, cloud infrastructure, deployment | Local dependency Compose file only |

No implemented path currently connects web → gateway → attendance → database → Kafka → reporting. Therefore the plan's latency, recovery, battery, and load targets are targets, not measured capabilities.

## 5. Concrete configuration and integration findings

### High priority: infrastructure connectivity

1. `infra/docker/docker-compose.yaml` mounts `./infra/docker/postgres-init.sql`. With the Compose file in `infra/docker`, the default relative resolution points beneath that directory again. Use a path relative to the Compose file, such as `./postgres-init.sql`, or explicitly establish a different project directory. Otherwise initialization will not mount the intended SQL file.
1. Schema Registry uses `kafka:19092`, but Kafka declares listeners at 9092, 29092, and 9093. The existing internal broker address is `kafka:29092`. Registry startup cannot reach the broker at its configured port.
1. Compose starts infrastructure only. It does not build or launch Java services, web, or the confidence service. A successful Compose syntax check cannot prove HRFlow is runnable.
1. Topic creation is manual and Kafka disables automatic topic creation. The topic script is not wired into a readiness-aware initialization flow. Retry and DLQ topics described in the plan are not provisioned.

### High priority: backend configuration and build consistency

1. Six `application.yaml` files contain properties syntax such as `spring.application.name=leave`. These are not YAML mappings defining the intended Spring property and may fail configuration loading. Attendance is the only service with a substantive YAML mapping.
1. The root POM uses Spring Boot parent 4.1.1; service POMs independently use 4.0.8. Services are reactor modules but do not inherit `hrflow-parent`, so its dependency management and shared properties do not govern them. The root README also declares a different version string, while the plan describes Boot 3. Resolve one supported version strategy explicitly.
1. No service depends on `hrflow-event-starter` or `hrflow-contracts`. The shared event setup therefore cannot affect service behavior in its current state.
1. The Avro plugin reads `${project.basedir}/../../contracts/events`, but the actual schema resides in `libs/hrflow-contracts/events`. Generation is pointed at the wrong directory.
1. The active shell provides Java 17 while the project targets Java 21. Maven `validate` succeeds because it does not compile Java. A full backend build was not established by this review.
1. Only attendance defines a service-specific server port and datasource. Other services lack the runtime configuration needed for the planned shared local environment; web-enabled services would otherwise compete for default ports when run together.

### Architectural and security gaps

1. `hrflow-event-starter` has no outbox relay, inbox handling, auto-configuration classes, retries, or correlation propagation. A resource named `application.yaml` in a library is not an adequate explicit starter configuration contract, especially once services have their own configuration files.
1. Schema selection through `hikari.schema` is a default search context, not authorization isolation. All schemas are created under a shared database setup; separate service credentials and grants are needed to enforce ownership. Tenant isolation within each service remains a separate requirement.
1. Security dependencies do not implement tenant identity, JWT validation, or authorization rules. The gateway has no configured security boundary. Business services need their own trusted tenant and actor context, including object-level authorization.
1. Prometheus is listed in attendance's endpoint exposure configuration, but the reviewed attendance POM does not include the Prometheus registry dependency. Endpoint exposure alone does not establish metrics export.

## 6. Event contract design

The single schema, `attendance-checked-in.v1.avsc`, contains event ID, tenant ID, employee ID, occurrence time, source, and optional reason. It is a useful starting record but does not match the plan's generic envelope: type, aggregate ID, correlation ID, and payload are absent. No producer or consumer uses it yet.

The schema models a check-in fact while the provisioned attendance topics model evidence, session, and daily status. Define which topic carries the schema and whether a check-in is a distinct event or a session transition. Otherwise topic names and contracts will diverge before integration begins.

The partition-key rule also needs refinement. `tenantId:employeeId` makes sense for employee streams, but shifts and holidays are not employee aggregates. Compacted topics retain the latest value per key, so their keys must identify the reference entity, such as tenant plus shift ID. One universal employee key is unsuitable for the complete catalog.

Before adding producers, define event time versus effective time, aggregate revision, deletion/tombstone behavior, schema compatibility policy, and projection rebuild procedures. Inbox deduplication prevents duplicate application; it does not by itself prevent a stale event from overwriting a newer projection.

The outbox must publish at least once safely: claim rows, publish, acknowledge broker success, then mark delivery. A crash after broker acknowledgment can still produce a duplicate, which is why consumer deduplication remains necessary. Specify retry exhaustion, DLQ ownership, and operational replay procedures alongside the implementation.

## 7. Python confidence service

This is the only component with meaningful application behavior and tests. FastAPI exposes `/health`, `/model`, and `/score`. Pydantic validates numeric ranges. The score uses twelve evidence features and returns confidence, decision, source, model version, and feature effects. A mock-location flag forces confidence to zero. Without artifact files, the service falls back to a weighted rules score.

Training compares logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting using cross-validation, prefers logistic regression unless boosting improves AUC by more than 0.01, calibrates the chosen classifier, selects an automatic-inference threshold, and writes model metadata. This is a sensible prototype pipeline with centralized feature order.

Important limitations:

- **Evaluation leakage:** `training/train.py` chooses the automatic threshold using `X_te/y_te` and reports automatic precision on the same data. Those metrics do not constitute an untouched final evaluation of the decision policy. Use separate training, calibration/threshold-selection, and final evaluation data.
- **Threshold fallback:** when no threshold meets target precision, training uses 0.95 anyway. That value has no established precision guarantee. Disable automatic inference when validation does not justify a threshold.
- **Threshold rounding:** metrics use the unrounded threshold, while saved metadata rounds it to three decimals. Evaluate the exact persisted policy.
- **Artifact evidence:** metadata reports 4,000 rows, ROC-AUC 0.9437, automatic precision 0.9669, and automatic coverage 0.785. The repository provides a synthetic generator and demo instructions, but metadata does not record dataset provenance. These numbers do not establish real employee attendance accuracy.
- **Dependency reproducibility:** Python requirements use unbounded minimum versions. Training locally under Python 3.14 and serving from a Python 3.12 Docker image with freshly resolved packages creates serialization compatibility risk. Record the training environment and pin compatible serving dependencies.
- **Fallback is partial:** missing files trigger rules mode; corrupt or incompatible artifact loading and prediction errors do not. The comment describing a safety net overstates current behavior.
- **Rules differ:** direct `rules_score` returns 0.05 for spoofing while the model wrapper returns 0.0. The public API uses the wrapper, but the discrepancy should be explicit or unified.
- **Weak identity validation:** tenant and employee IDs accept arbitrary strings, and `workDate` is an unrestricted string. There is no authentication or authorization on these endpoints.
- **Limited explanations:** model effects are baseline occlusion differences, not causal explanations. Rules-only responses have no explanatory reasons.
- **Testing scope:** tests cover health, one positive case, a phone-left case, spoof blocking, and a single invalid input. They do not explicitly test missing-model mode, damaged artifacts, metadata compatibility, or threshold selection failure.

The service is not connected to attendance, Kafka, or Compose. Integrating it through synchronous service-to-service HTTP would contradict the plan's Kafka-only rule. Choose an asynchronous evidence/result contract, an embedded rules path, or a documented architectural exception before integration. Keep inference outside the manual check-in transaction.

## 8. Documentation quality

`docs/Plan.md` is the substantive design document. It defines scope, ownership, resilience principles, targets, and a demo sequence. Its explicit cut line and failure-oriented tests are useful.

`docs/Achitecture.MD` and `docs/RestAPI-Database-Design.md` are empty. `docs/adr` and `.github/workflows` are empty. The root README is too short to reproduce the environment, and the web README is generic Nuxt starter documentation.

Decisions requiring reconciliation are React versus Nuxt/Vue, Boot 3 versus the two Boot 4 parent versions, JSON Schema/AsyncAPI versus Avro/Schema Registry, and how a separate ML service fits Kafka-only communication. Record actual decisions in ADRs and distinguish planned capabilities from implemented ones.

The API/database document should next define tenant and actor context, endpoints and error shape, pagination, idempotency behavior, per-service tables, unique constraints, approval transitions, outbox/inbox structure, retention, and migration ownership. These details are prerequisites for coherent implementation rather than documentation polish.

## 9. Verification performed

| Check | Result | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Python: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` from confidence-service | 5 passed, 1 dependency deprecation warning | Existing API examples work with the local model/environment |
| Python tests invoked from repository root | Import collection failed | Imports depend on service working directory; documented service-local invocation passes |
| Web: `npm run build` | Passed | Current Nuxt starter builds for production |
| Maven: `mvn -o validate` | Passed for all 10 reactor projects | POM/reactor validation only; no Java compilation or service startup |
| Docker Compose: `config --quiet` | Passed | Compose syntax valid; connectivity and mounted initialization not verified |
| Topic script: `bash -n` | Passed | Shell syntax valid; broker provisioning not executed |

Containers were not started, cloud resources were not provisioned, and no load, security, tenant-isolation, or end-to-end tests were run. The existing Git working tree contained substantial uncommitted work before review; conclusions apply to that working tree rather than a clean committed release.

## 10. Recommended implementation sequence

1. **Make the foundation reproducible.** Align Maven inheritance/version policy and Java 21 setup; correct YAML, Avro source path, Compose mount, and Registry listener; assign service ports; provide explicit startup instructions and dependency readiness checks.
1. **Decide the MVP architecture.** The existing service boundaries can remain, but with one backend/web/infrastructure developer, seven independently deployed services plus Kafka and Kubernetes are a substantial delivery burden. Concentrate on identity, attendance, and one downstream projection first. Merge reporting with notification if the schedule requires, as the plan already permits.
1. **Implement the event foundation.** Versioned contract, database migrations, transactional outbox, idempotent inbox, revision-aware consumers, retry/DLQ behavior, and integration tests proving crash/duplicate recovery.
1. **Deliver the first vertical workflow.** Authenticate an employee, resolve trusted tenant context, check in with an idempotency key, persist evidence/session/outbox atomically, publish an attendance event, and show the resulting status in the actual Nuxt UI. Prove cross-tenant access is rejected.
1. **Complete attendance rules.** Shifts, grace periods, holidays, checkout, corrections, cutoff-based absence, effective dates, and overnight/time-zone cases. Then measure the stated p95 and dashboard latency targets.
1. **Add leave and requests.** Explicit transition tables, authorization, balance consistency, duplicate approval handling, and compensating conflict behavior.
1. **Add delivery and operations.** CI checks, image builds, migration strategy, structured logs, operational metrics, failure recovery, backups, and one reproducible deployment environment before expanding cloud topology.
1. **Integrate inference after manual attendance is reliable.** Begin with auditable rules and employee confirmation. Establish labeled real-world evaluation and an isolated final test set before enabling automatic decisions based on model confidence.

The most valuable acceptance test now is: one employee from tenant A checks in twice with the same idempotency key, exactly one session is persisted, downstream delivery survives a stopped consumer, and a tenant B user cannot read or modify that session. Passing this demonstrates the central promises of the architecture more effectively than adding more empty service modules.

## Continued reference

### 3.1 Report schema refinements and critical failures

ReportRow is a shared envelope, not permission to return arbitrary shapes. Route-specific columns:

| Report | Additional typed fields |
|---|---|
| Attendance summary | workDate/date or month/string, departmentId/uuid?, present/int, late/int, absent/int, onLeave/int, workedMinutes/int |
| Late ranking | employeeId/uuid, fullName/string, lateMinutes/int, lateDays/int |
| Leave summary | leaveTypeId/uuid, departmentId/uuid?, days/decimal, requestCount/int |
| Request summary | typeId/uuid, status/string, count/int, averageCycleHours/decimal? |

`ReportRow.dimension/period/count` is the common projection shape; route refinements above are required in machine contracts, not inferred by clients. A post-commit connection failure on check-in is retried with the same key and yields the same session ID. A second key with an open session returns SESSION_ALREADY_OPEN, not a second interval. Leave approval while balance/request version changes yields 412/409, never a second debit. Provider/Registry downtime cannot change a committed resource response into a rolled-back business fact. If required local org projections are unavailable/stale, return 503 REFERENCE_NOT_READY and Retry-After; do not call identity for fallback. Cancellation after a newer approval/conflict revision requires fresh state and a new explicit command. Static paths such as `/requests/inbox` and `/leave/requests/pending` take precedence over `{id}` routes.

### 3.2 Implemented confidence prototype

Not part of the public gateway catalog. Source: `ml/confidence-service/confidence/api.py`. `GET /health` returns status/modelVersion; `GET /model` returns metadata; `POST /score` returns IDs/date plus confidence/decision/source/modelVersion/reasons. Evidence input is tenantId/employeeId/workDate strings and the twelve numeric features listed in `confidence/features.py`. Current validation includes numeric bounds but not authenticated tenant scope or typed date/UUID semantics; invalid numeric inputs return FastAPI 422, not the business error envelope. No auth, gateway route, outbox, or Kafka integration exists; do not deploy it publicly as-is. See [prototype limitations](../Architecture.md).

# Contracts reference 09

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## 4. Persistence specification

### 4.1 Normative conventions

All SQL below is **proposed PostgreSQL 16 DDL**, not existing Flyway migrations. Tables are created in dependency order within each schema. Every tenant-owned row has non-null `tenant_id`; the tenant root itself uses `id` as the tenant identifier. No FK crosses service schemas. Foreign employee/user IDs are local projection references or opaque audited actor IDs. All ordinary entity primary keys are `(tenant_id,id)`; natural/composite projections explicitly state their key. Mutable tables add `created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK(version>0)`. Immutable tables add only created_at; normal runtime grants prohibit UPDATE/DELETE on evidence, ledger, decision-action, and audit tables. Application writes maintain updated_at/version atomically; no trigger behavior is assumed. An immutable request for correction is distinct from its mutable summary/projection: the action ledger preserves decisions. All tenant FK references include tenant_id; UUID uniqueness by itself is not an authorization boundary. `uuid` IDs are generated by the application; no database UUIDv7 extension is assumed. Notations use actual SQL nullability: omitted NOT NULL means nullable. PK columns are inherently NOT NULL. JSONB columns are bounded and validated by typed application schemas; jsonb type alone is not payload validation. Foreign IDs to other services have no FK, but are checked against local ref tables where available.

Retention profiles (periods require O05 approval):

| Profile | Tables | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| MASTER | Org/types/catalogue/templates | Soft-delete when referenced; purge/pseudonymize only through authorized retention job |
| BUSINESS | Sessions/requests/corrections/days/steps | Preserve audited history; legal period unresolved; no normal hard-delete API |
| SENSITIVE | Raw evidence/attachments/device tokens | Minimum permitted period, then controlled erase; consent and access audit |
| AUDIT | Ledger/decision actions/audit_log | Append-only application writes; protected archival/retention operations |
| PROJECTION | Ref/fact/summary tables | Rebuildable; retain source revision and refresh watermark |
| DELIVERY | Notifications/attempts/jobs | User-visible retention and signed-object cleanup; exact periods unresolved |
| TRANSIT | Outbox/inbox/idempotency | Pending rows never discarded; dedupe must cover replay horizon; command keys ≥30 days proposed |

The per-table purpose, constraints, and query indexes follow; common tenant filtering, retention, audit, and migration rules apply to every table. Every mutation of a BUSINESS/MASTER resource writes its owner's audit_log and, where cataloged, outbox in the same transaction. No cascade delete removes business evidence. FK defaults are restrictive. RLS is proposed defense-in-depth, not included in this DDL; runtime role grants and transaction-local tenant handling require integration tests.

Create schemas with a migration/admin role first; runtime roles must not own the entire database.

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS identity_org;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS attendance;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS leave;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS request;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS notification;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS reporting;
```


### 4.2 Owner tables and DDL

### identityorg.tenant

Owner: `identity_org` service schema. Purpose: Tenant root; id itself is the isolation key.

Retention: MASTER; mutable current state; owner audit and version preconditions required.

PK and all FK/unique/check constraints are declared below; listed indexes serve tenant-scoped lookups/queues. If no extra index is listed, the primary/unique index serves the expected access path.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "identity_org"."tenant" (
  id uuid NOT NULL,
  name text NOT NULL,
  slug text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  timezone text NOT NULL,
  country char(2) NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE','SUSPENDED')),
  deleted_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
```


### identityorg.appuser

Owner: `identity_org` service schema. Purpose: Tenant login identity, never password/token plaintext.

Retention: MASTER; mutable current state; owner audit and version preconditions required.

PK and all FK/unique/check constraints are declared below; listed indexes serve tenant-scoped lookups/queues. If no extra index is listed, the primary/unique index serves the expected access path.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "identity_org"."app_user" (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  id uuid NOT NULL,
  email text NOT NULL,
  password_hash text NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE','DISABLED')),
  last_login_at timestamptz,
  deleted_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,id),
  UNIQUE (tenant_id,email),
  FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES identity_org.tenant(id)
);
```


### identityorg.userrole

Owner: `identity_org` service schema. Purpose: Explicit role assignments, no implied OWNER inheritance.

Retention: MASTER; mutable current state; owner audit and version preconditions required.

PK and all FK/unique/check constraints are declared below; listed indexes serve tenant-scoped lookups/queues. If no extra index is listed, the primary/unique index serves the expected access path.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "identity_org"."user_role" (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  user_id uuid NOT NULL,
  role text NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('OWNER','HR_ADMIN','MANAGER','EMPLOYEE')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,user_id,role),
  FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id,user_id) REFERENCES "identity_org"."app_user" (tenant_id,id)
```

# Contracts reference 02

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## 2. Reusable schemas and endpoint profiles

### 2.1 Schema notation

In schema declarations, `?` means nullable/optional; arrays use `[]`; all other fields are required unless stated as response-only. IDs/timestamps in examples are illustrative. Resource examples are representative minimal wire shapes, not existing DTOs. Resource outputs include ID, version, createdAt, updatedAt for mutable aggregates; immutable facts use ID/createdAt without a fictional update lifecycle. List schemas wrap the named resource in the section 1.2 envelope. Jobs return id/status/statusUrl, with READY downloadUrl only after authorization. Nested references below are within the same tenant; no cross-service foreign key is implied.

### Empty

No request body.

tenantSlug:string; email:string; password:string (write-only).

```json
  "email": "employee@example.test",
  "password": "example-only-secret"
}
```

# Architecture reference 03

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## 23. Reliability and recovery runbooks

| Failure | Detect | Immediate behavior | Recover and verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway down | Health/HTTP failure | Clients retain pending keys | Restore container/config; replay same key, verify one resource |
| PostgreSQL down | Connection/commit errors | No false success; 503/retry | Restore DB; inspect uncertain commits by key |
| Kafka down | Relay errors/backlog | Local commands commit while bounded capacity remains | Recover broker; drain ordered outbox; compare IDs |
| Consumer killed | Lag/no heartbeat | Other services continue | Restart; inbox dedupe; verify one logical effect |
| Provider down | Attempt failures | Inbox persists, external delivery pending | Retry with backoff; distinguish unknown acceptance |
| Duplicate event | Inbox unique conflict | No repeated mutation | Acknowledge; compare state/ledger |
| Delayed event | Revision/time lag | Guard snapshot; flag stale | Apply newer revision/recompute; preserve history |
| Poison schema | Consumer error/quarantine | Block affected aggregate or quarantine safely | Fix reader/schema; audited replay original event ID |
| Outbox backlog | Age/disk growth | Degraded async status; bounded admission | Fix broker/head; reconcile status counts |
| Failed migration | Deployment job fails | Do not deploy incompatible code | Forward fix or compatible image rollback; clean DB test |
| Corrupt projection | Reconciliation mismatch | Mark stale/disable affected export | Shadow rebuild, compare, switch atomically |
| Object storage down | Upload/export errors | No READY file claim | Retry job; verify checksum/access/expiry |
| Bad deployment | Smoke/error regression | Stop rollout | Known digest/config rollback if schema compatible |
| Host/region loss | Infrastructure monitoring | Pilot outage; disclose scope | Restore backups to new target; rehydrate broker/projections |

Proposed pilot recovery objectives are RPO ≤24 hours and RTO ≤4 hours, pending business agreement and successful restore exercise. They are recommendations, not existing guarantees; actual backup frequency/restore speed determines feasibility. Broker replay cannot recover business facts that were never backed up in the owner database. Restore exercises verify tenant counts, ledger consistency, object references, outbox/inbox state, and access-key validity. Do not replay old notifications to real users during recovery validation.

## 24. Performance and capacity engineering

Keep check-in to bounded local queries, employee guard/session write, idempotency write, and outbox insert. No provider call, cross-service lookup, model prediction, or report aggregation belongs in that transaction. Index tenant/employee/open-session and employee/work-date lookups. Measure lock contention separately for duplicate submissions from the same employee. Export workers use a separate bounded pool/queue so CSV generation cannot starve attendance connections. Kafka throughput depends on partition skew, serialization, broker I/O, DB writes, and consumer batch behavior. Size partitions from measured throughput and future migration cost, not solely current script defaults. Evidence batch limits prevent one phone from monopolizing a transaction.

Load fixture: at least two tenants, distinct employees, active assignments, holidays, and leave cases. Run warm-up followed by a recorded steady-state window; report sample count, p50/p95/p99, throughput, error codes, hardware, pool sizes, and payload size. Include network loss after commit, duplicate keys, same-employee races, stopped consumers, and broker downtime. Dashboard propagation measurement correlates source event commit with applied projection and client render acknowledgment in test tooling. No existing benchmark establishes the original targets.

## 25. Testing strategy and ownership

| Layer | Primary owner | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Domain unit | A | Shift/date/status, transitions, balance arithmetic, overlap |
| Repository/migration | A | PostgreSQL constraints, locks, clean/upgrade migration |
| Kafka contract | A with B review | Envelope/payload fixtures, compatibility, keys, revisions |
| API integration | A | Role/resource/tenant, idempotency, If-Match, errors |
| Mobile unit/offline | B | Stable queued keys, refresh serialization, permission denial |
| Web interaction/accessibility | A | Empty/error/stale states, filters, keyboard workflows |
| End-to-end | A+B | Login → check-in → projection → approval → export |
| Security | A, independent review before launch | Tenant substitution, token/header abuse, file access |
| Recovery/load | A with B device validation | Kill consumer, restart relay, restore, 100-client run |

Use Testcontainers for PostgreSQL/Kafka integration where practical, not mocks for transaction/offset guarantees. Duplicate test: deliver one event twice, assert one ledger/projection/notification effect. Out-of-order test: revision 4 then 3, assert revision 4 remains. Saga test: approve, stop attendance, cancel, resume; older approval must not resurrect leave. Kill-consumer test: stop notification, check in successfully, restart, catch up, assert one logical inbox item. Crash-relay test: send acknowledgment then kill before published mark; verify duplicate is harmless. Tenant test includes count endpoints, reports, SSE reconnect, attachments, and background jobs. Current coverage is only five confidence API tests; no percentages are claimed.

## 26. Evolution, simplifications, and decision gates

MVP keeps one database instance, one local broker, polling outbox, and a narrow end-to-end slice. Do not add Redis, service mesh, Debezium, Kafka Streams, or EKS merely to match an enterprise checklist. Merge reporting into a notification projections module if delivery pressure warrants, preserving logical ownership and contracts. Extract services only when independent load, ownership, deployment cadence, or fault isolation justifies operational overhead. Scale broker/DB topology after measured saturation or agreed availability requirements. Adopt evidence partitioning after measured retention/index pressure. Adopt ML only after permitted evidence, real labels, calibration, and policy review.

### 26.1 Confidence prototype disposition

`ml/confidence-service` implements `/health`, `/model`, and `/score` with twelve features and a mock-location hard block. It loads a joblib model if both artifacts exist; missing artifacts use rules, but corrupt artifacts/prediction errors are not handled as a complete fallback. Five tests pass in its own directory; root invocation needs import-path packaging work. Training selects threshold on the same holdout used to report automatic precision; a separate final evaluation set is required. If no threshold meets target precision, fallback 0.95 does not establish safe automatic inference. Saved threshold rounding and unpinned dependencies can change deployed decisions. Metadata does not establish real-data provenance; synthetic demo metrics are not pilot accuracy. The Python 3.12 image and local Python 3.14 environment require a pinned artifact compatibility check. No Kafka integration exists; asynchronous scoring result contracts would be a separate proposed extension. A vision service is optional future work and is removed from mandatory week-12 delivery.

### 26.2 Open questions

| ID | Decision | Owner and deadline | Safe interim behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| O01 | Nuxt versus original React plan | A+B, week 1 | Keep scaffold; no framework rewrite |
| O02 | Holiday/leave/manual precedence, late+early mapping, conflict balance handling | Product/HR+A, before leave integration | Preserve evidence, flag conflicts, no automatic resolution |
| O03 | Correction window, pending inference expiry, overnight/DST support | Product/HR+A+B, week 2 | Same-day shifts; explicit review; no guessed finalization |
| O04 | Pilot hosting and operational budget | A/operator, week 5 | Local demo; no EKS mandate |
| O05 | Privacy basis, consent, retention/erasure, recovery objectives | Tenant owner/security/operator, before real data | Synthetic data only |
| O06 | Avro envelope/Registry versus simpler JSON contract | A+B, week 1 | Existing Avro remains prototype; no incompatible publication |
| O07 | Final Boot parent inheritance and tested toolchain | A, week 1 | Do not alter versions for documentation |
| O08 | Auth lifetimes, revocation window, platform provisioning credential | Security+A, week 2 | Proposed short access tokens; block launch without review |

## 27. Appendices and traceability

### 27.1 Decision index

- [ADR-001: Service and event boundaries](../adr/001-SERVICE-AND-EVENT-BOUNDARIES.md).
- [ADR-002: Tenant and persistence isolation](../adr/002-TENANT-AND-PERSISTENCE-ISOLATION.md).
- [ADR-003: Event delivery and contracts](../adr/003-EVENT-DELIVERY-AND-CONTRACTS.md).
- [ADR-004: Attendance and leave conflicts](../adr/004-ATTENDANCE-AND-LEAVE-CONFLICTS.md).
- [ADR-005: Deployment and client baseline](../adr/005-DEPLOYMENT-AND-CLIENT-BASELINE.md).

### 27.2 Requirement traceability

| ID | Requirement | Design | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | Auth and tenant isolation | Sections 6–7, 17 | Tenant/header/JWT/object tests |
| R02 | Organization/calendar | Section 7 | Effective assignment and holiday projection fixtures |
| R03 | Durable check-in/out | Section 8 | Atomic write, duplicate key, concurrent open-session tests |
| R04 | Event recovery | Sections 13–14 | Relay crash, inbox duplicate, order/kill-consumer tests |
| R05 | Leave approvals and balances | Section 9 | Locking/reservation/saga/cancel tests |
| R06 | General requests | Section 10 | Chain/version/participant/fulfillment tests |
| R07 | Notifications/live views | Sections 11–12 | Inbox dedupe, SSE reconnect, freshness assertions |
| R08 | Audit/corrections | Sections 8, 15, 17 | Append-only decisions and actor/reason tests |
| R09 | Reports/exports | Section 12 | Projection rebuild, authorized CSV, URL expiry |
| R10 | Reproducible deployment | Sections 20–23 | Fresh setup, smoke, rollback, restore rehearsal |
| R11 | Nudges/inference | Sections 8, 18, 26 | Permission/device/battery/labeled evaluation; should/stretch |
| R12 | Performance | Sections 3, 24 | Recorded 100-client latency/propagation report |

### 27.3 Configuration inventory

| Setting | Current evidence | Target handling |
|---|---|---|
| Java | POM target 21; review shell Java 17 | CI/dev Java 21 toolchain gate |
| Boot | Root 4.1.1, service 4.0.8 | One reviewed inheritance policy |
| Cloud | Gateway 2025.1.3 | Verify compatible Boot baseline and test gateway |
| PostgreSQL | Compose 16, `hrflow` local credentials | Secret-managed distinct runtime/migration roles |
| Kafka | Compose 3.8.0, host 9092/internal 29092 | Private secure listener in deployment |
| Registry | Compose 8.0.0; serializer property 8.1.0 | Verify image/client compatibility, fix listener |
| Avro | 1.11.4; wrong generation directory | Correct path and compatibility fixtures |
| Web | Nuxt ^4.6.1, Vue ^3.5.43, router ^5.4.0 | Existing npm lockfile governs resolved build |
| Confidence | Unbounded Python minima, Python 3.12 image | Pin serving/training versions if included |
| Ports | Attendance currently 8082 | Target gateway 8080, services 8101–8106, confidence 8107 |
| Secrets | Hard-coded local DB values | External environment/secret store; never commit production values |

Environment variable names are not standardized today; implementation must document actual Spring binding/secret mounts rather than assume these target controls exist.

### 27.4 Glossary

ADR: architecture decision record. ACL: access-control list. API: application programming interface. DLQ: dead-letter queue/topic. DTO: data-transfer object. IAM: identity and access management. JWT: JSON Web Token. JWKS: JSON Web Key Set. RBAC: role-based access control. RLS: row-level security. RPO: recovery point objective. RTO: recovery time objective. SLO: service-level objective. SSE: Server-Sent Events. UTC: coordinated universal time. A projection is derived data, an aggregate is a consistency boundary, and an inbox is a durable consumer deduplication record.

### 27.5 External compatibility references

Checked 2026-10-22: [Spring Cloud compatibility matrix](https://spring.io/projects/spring-cloud/) lists 2025.1.x with Boot 4.0.x and 4.1.x starting with 2025.1.2. [Spring Boot system requirements](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/system-requirements.html) lists Java 17 as the framework minimum for 4.1.1; this repository independently targets Java 21. The observed parent mismatch is therefore a governance/reproducibility issue, not proof that Cloud 2025.1.3 is incompatible. Repository dependencies were not upgraded, and full application startup compatibility remains unverified.

# Contracts reference 16

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## 5. Event contract catalog

### 5.1 Shared envelope and processing contract

Status: proposed normalized contracts. The only existing machine schema is the legacy flat `AttendanceCheckedIn` Avro record. All catalog entries below use this envelope; every field is required except nullable causationId.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| eventId | uuid | Stable publication/deduplication ID, never regenerated for relay/retry |
| type | string | Allowlisted past-tense event fact with `.v1` suffix |
| schemaVersion | integer, exactly 1 | Envelope major version |
| tenantId | uuid | Producer-validated owner tenant |
| aggregateId | string | Stable owner aggregate ID; composite IDs use canonical colon-separated UUID/date components |
| aggregateVersion | positive bigint | Monotonic revision of aggregate, not Kafka offset or timestamp |
| occurredAt | UTC instant | Owner commit/fact time for snapshots; evidence observation time also in payload |
| correlationId | uuid | Originating request/job chain |
| causationId | uuid or null | Triggering event or durable command ID |
| payload | typed object | Exact topic/type payload below; no arbitrary entity serialization |

Every entry inherits: delivery at least once; idempotency is consumer-name + tenantId + eventId inbox; snapshot upserts additionally guard aggregateVersion. ### 5.13 Legacy schema and optional events

Existing `AttendanceCheckedIn` Avro fields: eventId/UUID logical string, tenantId/string, employeeId/string, occurredAt/timestamp-millis, source/MANUAL|NUDGE|INFERRED, reason/nullable string. It lacks generic envelope fields and its MANUAL versus API TAP semantics differ. Do not silently reinterpret MANUAL. Before publication, choose a new normalized schema/topic migration or preserve legacy producer/consumer adapters with explicit mapping. Optional `notification.sent.v1` is deferred: provider acceptance is not delivery, and no MVP consumer needs the event. Vision/camera producers and ML scoring topics are not approved; a future ADR must define consent, payloads, and asynchronous result behavior.

## 6. Contract authority and machine-readable evolution

No OpenAPI/AsyncAPI files or generators exist in the inspected repository. These Markdown contracts define planned behavior; no mock server is claimed to have been generated. Proposed source strategy: API OpenAPI files per owning service and Avro event schemas under hrflow-contracts, with an AsyncAPI routing/catalog index if Avro is retained. Choose serialization in O06 before expanding schemas; avoid JSON and Avro catalogs that disagree on field authority. Week 1 delivers machine-readable contracts and mock examples for auth/check-in/today first; remaining endpoints expand alongside features. CI should parse schemas, validate examples, run compatibility fixtures, and verify controller/event producers against those contracts. This documentation revision does not add speculative machine contracts for all 112 routes before domain decisions are approved.

## 7. Cross-contract correctness gates

- Tenant row predicates, composite constraints, resource authorization, and safe background context are all necessary; tenant_id alone is insufficient.
- Guard/lock and state predicates enforce balance/approval atomicity; outbox is in that same local transaction.
- Offset acknowledgment follows local commit; broker idempotence does not create exactly-once database/provider effects.
- Outbox cleanup and inbox retention account for replay; full snapshots plus owner exports permit rebuild.
- Historical evidence and audit are append-only in normal use; controlled privacy retention is separately authorized.
- Attachment presign is not attachment approval; quarantine/READY is mandatory before sensitive download/use.
- Full snapshot payloads and higher revisions protect projections from out-of-order events.
- `syncState=APPLIED` requires actual attendance acknowledgment/reconciliation evidence; until that protocol exists use PENDING/UNKNOWN/CONFLICT, never guess APPLIED.
- Asynchronous exports/year-end have status endpoints and persisted jobs.
- O02/O03/O05/O06/O08 must be resolved or the dependent capability remains disabled before real-user launch.

# Contracts reference 03

> **Warning:** Superseded historical design; use the current parent specification and roadmap. No feature is implemented by this reference.

## Continued reference

### Audit

id:uuid; actorId:uuid?; action:string; entity:string; entityId:uuid?; diff:bounded safe object; at:instant.

```json
{
  "id": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "actorId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "action": "EMPLOYEE_UPDATED",
  "entity": "employee",
  "entityId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "diff": {
    "fullName": "Updated Employee"
  },
  "at": "2026-10-22T01:00:00Z"
}
```


### CheckIn

deviceId:string; occurredAt:instant; source:TAP|NUDGE; latitude?:number; longitude?:number; accuracyM?:number >=0; employee comes from token; manual source forbidden.

```json
{
  "deviceId": "installation-example",
  "occurredAt": "2026-10-22T01:00:00Z",
  "source": "TAP"
}
```


### CheckOut

sessionId:uuid; occurredAt:instant; deviceId:string; checkout >= check-in; session owned by caller.

```json
{
  "sessionId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "occurredAt": "2026-10-22T10:00:00Z",
  "deviceId": "installation-example"
}
```


### Session

id:uuid; employeeId:uuid; workDate:date; checkInAt:instant; checkOutAt:instant?; source:TAP|NUDGE|INFERRED|MANUAL; confidence:number? 0..1; reason:string?; confirmStatus:NONE|PENDING|CONFIRMED|REJECTED; effective:boolean; version:int.

```json
{
  "id": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "employeeId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "workDate": "2026-10-22",
  "checkInAt": "2026-10-22T01:00:00Z",
  "checkOutAt": null,
  "source": "TAP",
  "confidence": null,
  "reason": null,
  "confirmStatus": "NONE",
  "effective": true,
  "version": 1
}
```


### EvidenceBatch

items:EvidenceInput[1..100]; all-or-nothing admission; item eventId is stable across batch retries.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "eventId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
      "kind": "TAP",
      "occurredAt": "2026-10-22T01:00:00Z",
      "deviceId": "installation-example",
      "payload": {}
    }
  ]
}
```


### EvidenceInput

eventId:uuid; kind:TAP|MANUAL|GEOFENCE_ENTER|GEOFENCE_EXIT|WIFI|BLE; occurredAt:instant; deviceId:string; latitude?:number; longitude?:number; accuracyM?:number; payload:bounded object. MANUAL accepted only via HR/correction server path.

```json
{
  "eventId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "kind": "TAP",
  "occurredAt": "2026-10-22T01:00:00Z",
  "deviceId": "installation-example",
  "payload": {}
}
```


### EvidenceReceipt

acceptedIds:uuid[]; duplicates:uuid[]; no automatic attendance conclusion implied.

```json
{
  "acceptedIds": [
    "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020"
  ],
  "duplicates": []
}
```


### Evidence

EvidenceInput plus id:uuid, receivedAt:instant, employeeId:uuid, provenance:string; raw coordinates restricted to HR.

```json
{
  "id": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "eventId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "employeeId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "kind": "TAP",
  "occurredAt": "2026-10-22T01:00:00Z",
  "receivedAt": "2026-10-22T01:00:00Z",
  "deviceId": "installation-example",
  "payload": {},
  "provenance": "AUTHENTICATED_DEVICE"
}
```


### Today

workDate:date; shift:Shift?; sessions:Session[]; dailyStatus:DailyStatus?; nextAction:CHECK_IN|CHECK_OUT|REVIEW|NONE.

```json
{
  "workDate": "2026-10-22",
  "shift": null,
  "sessions": [],
  "dailyStatus": null,
  "nextAction": "REVIEW"
}
```


### DailyStatus

employeeId:uuid; workDate:date; status:PRESENT|LATE|ABSENT|LEAVE_EARLY|ON_LEAVE|HOLIDAY|DAY_OFF; dayType:string; attendanceState:string; late:boolean; earlyLeave:boolean; workedMinutes:int?; reviewRequired:boolean; version:int.

```json
{
  "employeeId": "019a0000-0000-7000-8000-000000000020",
  "workDate": "2026-10-22",
  "status": "PRESENT",
  "dayType": "WORKING",
  "attendanceState": "OPEN",
  "late": false,
  "earlyLeave": false,
  "workedMinutes": null,
  "reviewRequired": false,
  "version": 1
}
```


### Reason

reason:string non-empty ≤2000; approval may use optional note instead as specified.
