# Hardware and hosting assessment

## Observed local host

| Item | Observed evidence | Status | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Model | `sysctl -n hw.model`: Mac16,12 | **Verified** | User confirms this is production machine |
| Memory | `sysctl -n hw.memsize`: 17179869184 bytes | **Verified** 16 GiB | Load test before pilot |
| CPU | `sysctl -n hw.ncpu`: 10 | **Verified** logical CPU count | Do not infer exact marketed processor |
| OS | `sw_vers`: macOS 26.5.1 | **Verified** | Docker starts only after user login unless proven otherwise |
| Disk | `df -h .`: about 5.1 GiB free, 98 percent capacity | **Blocked** | At least 30 GiB free before pulls; 50 GiB preferred |
| Docker | CLI 29.6.2, Compose v5.5.1; daemon absent | **Partial** | Desktop startup/reboot demonstrated |
| Backup disk | No external disk confirmed | **Unknown** | Dedicated mounted destination with free space and restore test |
| Public IP/router/ISP | Not inspected or provided | **Unknown** | Tunnel path selected; no router forwarding |
| Domain | Not provided | **Unknown** | Owned domain and DNS control before public TLS |

The disk threshold is a conservative pilot requirement, not a measurement of HRFlow's future footprint. Do not delete user files automatically. Review storage in macOS settings, archive with owner agreement, and rerun the disk check.

## Check each unknown

1. Confirm whether this computer is the production host and can remain powered and awake during agreed hours.
1. Inspect disk health in Disk Utility First Aid and record result; do not run repair during development without a backup.
1. Ask the ISP/router administrator for WAN address type, inbound restrictions, CGNAT, dynamic IP behavior, and router ownership. Compare router WAN IP with an external-IP site privately; do not paste addresses in this repo.
1. Run a browser bandwidth test at the host; record upload/download and latency privately, then test with two phones on different networks.
1. Verify firewall allows only approved ingress; inspect published Compose ports locally. Never expose PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker API, or Uptime Kuma publicly.
1. Mount the external backup disk and record path, capacity, encryption, ownership, and unplugged behavior privately. A directory existing at an unmounted path is not a mounted disk.
1. Simulate a short power/network interruption after a valid backup and synthetic data. Record startup order, recovery, and missed cron behavior.
1. Agree pilot user count; use 5 to 10 synthetic or consenting pilot users as a test scenario, not a capacity promise.

## Chosen access path

Use Cloudflare Tunnel because router/public-IP capability is unknown. Tunnel traffic is outbound; no port forwarding is configured. Caddy remains the internal reverse proxy. Cloudflare terminates public automatic TLS; Caddy serves a private origin listener reachable only by cloudflared. Caddy public ACME is not claimed through an unconfigured tunnel.

The free Tunnel path requires no paid Access plan for publishing an app; budget for a domain at its registrar's actual price. Existing power, internet, external disk, and replacement hardware still have costs. There is no free-tier uptime guarantee. Internet or Cloudflare failure removes remote access; the data remains on the host. LAN emergency access must remain authenticated and private.

[Caddy HTTPS requirements](https://caddyserver.com/docs/quick-starts/https) and [Cloudflare published applications](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/routing-to-tunnel/) were checked 2026-10-23. A verified directly reachable host is new evidence that can justify an access ADR change; do not operate both public paths accidentally.

## Hard launch blockers

Disk headroom, target JDK, running Docker, domain/DNS control, external backup target, production-host confirmation, and unattended reboot behavior are unresolved. If blocked in week 2, redeploy privately on the real host and mark remote exposure **FAIL** until prerequisites pass. Never call localhost on the development laptop a successful production deployment on another machine.

# Consolidation and client migration

## Inspect first

Read `pom.xml`, `services/attendance/pom.xml`, `services/api-gateway/pom.xml`, all application YAML files, and `web/package.json`. Verify again that business controllers/migrations are absent. If new code appears after this audit, inventory tests/routes before moving it.

## Safe migration order

1. Create a protected code checkpoint on the developer's weekly branch without including secrets or generated dependencies. The documentation branch is not an application checkpoint.
1. Create proposed `services/hrflow-app` using the current root Java 21/Boot 4.1.1 baseline; keep old service directories untouched until new app behavior and tests pass.
1. Retain domain names as packages and owner schemas. Initially implement only a database-backed diagnostic through private Caddy; never invent migrated behavior that did not exist.
1. Keep the root reactor until a deliberate build-profile change parks old scaffolds. Compile/test the new app explicitly; confirm no accidental launch of seven apps or broker stack.
1. Add Flyway migrations per schema in one ordered migration stream. Restrict repositories to owner packages; cross-domain reads use public module APIs or local projections, not cross-schema joins.
1. Write outbox in the domain transaction. A local scheduled dispatcher invokes independently idempotent notification/report handlers through application ports. Persist inbox plus effect in one transaction; mark completion only after all required handler receipts exist.
1. Preserve public `/api/v1` routes while OpenAPI becomes their single wire source. Controllers adapt domain objects to DTOs; do not publish JPA entities.
1. Preserve current Nuxt tree on a checkpoint, then create React sources in `web` on the build branch. Keep the lockfile only for its matching manifest; do not mix Nuxt dependencies into the React target.
1. B creates or locates Flutter source in proposed `mobile`; uses generated mock before backend is complete. Flutter dependency versions are selected and locked by B, not invented in docs.
1. Replace dependency-only Compose usage with proposed `infra/selfhost/compose.yaml`; app/PostgreSQL/Caddy only initially. Add private Kuma and tunnel connector after readiness. Keep old Compose as historical scaffolding, not production startup.

## Transaction and reliability change

Unlike the old distributed architecture, one JVM and one database can commit module operations locally. Keep domain ownership, audit, idempotency and outbox; do not imply Kafka acknowledgment or global exactly-once behavior. Dispatcher crash before receipt retries. Crash after handler commit finds inbox receipt. Provider sends remain outside DB transactions and can duplicate after timeout; in-app records are deduplicated.

## Contract and database reconciliation

Old endpoint coverage and owner schema names remain in reference documents. Replace owner service with owner package; runtime route is one app behind Caddy, port 8080 internally. Keep tenant constraints and no cross-module SQL joins. Proposed old outbox/inbox DDL is adapted to local handler receipts before implementation; legacy Kafka topic definitions are deferred compatibility references, not runtime requirements.

## Return to safety

Never delete or reset old scaffolds to make the build green. Use a new branch from a green tag, inspect diffs, and migrate one package at a time. If a new path fails, keep the old tree and reduce the next change. The new app needs its own tested migrations; copying proposed documentation SQL without tests is not migration completion.

# Project baseline and capacity

## Inputs and honesty

The user replied “24” to the combined hours question. This guide interprets that as A 24 and B 24 hours per week; correct the dashboard if the answer meant only one contributor or 24 combined. Start date remains unknown. Working rhythm is Monday through Friday; steps last 45 to 60 minutes, or 30 to 45 in light weeks. Deadline is start plus exactly 84 calendar days, with release completed by the preceding Friday if needed.

Only 70 percent is planned: 16.8 hours each in ordinary weeks. Weeks 4 and 8 are 15 percent lighter: 14.28 hours each. No weekend work is allocated. Production setup is not ready, according to the user; host/domain/backup gates remain blocked.

## Capacity math

Normal weeks: 10 times 33.6 equals 336 combined hours. Light weeks: 2 times 28.56 equals 57.12. Total planned capacity is 393.12 contributor-hours; the unplanned 30 percent is not allocated secretly.

Ordinary weeks have 15 steps; Week 2 has 17 after the beginner dry-run split password, JWT and refresh into separate steps. There are 182 steps total. Ordinary weeks have ten A-owned-or-joint and seven B-owned-or-joint participations; Week 2 adds two A steps. Shared steps count for both. At maximum 60 minutes in normal weeks and 45 in light weeks, core upper estimate is 10 times 17 plus 2 times 12.75 plus 2 extra Week-2 auth steps equals 197.5 combined hours. Reading allowance is 2 hours each per week, 48 total. Planned buffer is 147.62 hours for diagnostics, review, recovery, pairing and slower learning.

A: 117 core plus 24 reading plus 55.56 buffer equals 196.56. B: 80.5 core plus 24 reading plus 92.06 buffer equals 196.56. B uses buffer for real-device/contract acceptance and pairing, not unreviewed backend architecture. These estimates are provisional; a junior step that cannot fit is split or carried forward, not called done.

## Architecture comparison

| Outcome | Core estimate basis | Combined estimate | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A seven deployables | C core plus seven-service wiring, broker, security and recovery work | 197.5 plus 180 overhead plus 48 learning plus 147.62 buffer | **FAIL** baseline mostly unbuilt |
| B two deployables | C core plus separate worker deployment, credentials and integration | 197.5 plus 70 overhead plus 48 learning plus 147.62 buffer | **FAIL** no demonstrated benefit |
| C modular monolith | Counted 182-step ledger, package boundaries, local outbox worker | 197.5 core plus 48 learning plus 147.62 buffer | **CONDITIONAL PASS** at interpreted 24 h each |

Overhead estimates are planning estimates, not measured velocity. C is selected because source is mostly unbuilt and it has the fewest runtime failure modes. If actual contributor hours are below 24 or week 1 velocity exceeds estimates, do not certify this full scope as feasible: replan explicit cuts while preserving security, correctness, and restore gates.

## Current safe checkpoint

There is no green application tag. Dashboard starts at W01-S01, status **Not run**. Documentation commits are not evidence that any weekly gate passed. User-staged source is preserved outside documentation commits.

# Phase 00 — Preparation and technical assessment

> **Navigation:** [Documentation root](../../README.md) · [Start here](../START-HERE.md) · [Dashboard](../YOU-ARE-HERE.md) · [Next: Week 01](../01-FOUNDATION/README.md)

## Objective and phase overview

Phase 00 establishes the technical, operational, and architectural foundation before active implementation begins. It prevents wasted development hours by auditing the starting repository state, verifying host hardware capabilities, calculating realistic team capacity, and outlining an incremental migration plan to the modular monolith.

No code modifications or container pulls should begin until the preparation assessments are completed and the prerequisite blockers are acknowledged.

## Preparation deliverables and documents

The preparation phase comprises five specialized engineering documents:

| Document | Primary focus | Key outcomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Repository audit](REPOSITORY-AUDIT.md) | Codebase and configuration inspection | Verified toolchain discrepancies, missing migrations, and prototype inventory. |
| [Project baseline and capacity](PROJECT-BASELINE.md) | Capacity math and velocity assumptions | 197.5 core hours mapped against 393.12 available hours across twelve weeks. |
| [Hardware and hosting assessment](HARDWARE-AND-HOSTING-ASSESSMENT.md) | Physical machine and network constraints | Mac16,12 host verified, 16 GiB RAM, 5.1 GiB free disk blocker identified. |
| [Migration plan](MIGRATION-PLAN.md) | Incremental migration to modular monolith | Safe transition from seven services to `services/hrflow-app` without data loss. |
| [Start here](../START-HERE.md) | Daily implementation workflow | 5-minute daily routine, 30–90 minute steps, and stop rules. |

## Pre-flight verification gates

Before launching Week 01 (Walking Skeleton), the following entry gates must be evaluated:

- [ ] Repository inspection complete; build discrepancies recorded.
- [ ] Available disk space reviewed; cleanup planned to reach at least 30 GiB free.

# Week 08 troubleshooting

> **Navigation:** [Previous: Week 07](../07-REQUESTS-AND-APPROVALS/README.md) · [You are here](../YOU-ARE-HERE.md) · [Next: Week 09](../09-REPORTING-AUDIT-OBSERVABILITY/README.md)

## Runtime never becomes ready

- Symptom: Compose app unhealthy or request refuses connection.
- Likely cause: Docker stopped, wrong JDK, migration error or database not ready.
- Diagnose: `docker compose -f infra/selfhost/compose.yaml ps`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Healthy app and PostgreSQL with no public DB binding.
- Fix: Check disk then Docker/JDK; inspect last safe log lines; correct one config on branch, never delete volume.
- Verify: Re-run readiness and current happy scenario.

## Schema or key assertion fails

- Symptom: Migration/constraint/idempotency test returns an unexpected failure.
- Likely cause: Applied migration edited, missing tenant/key predicate or stale fixture.
- Diagnose: `mvn -f services/hrflow-app/pom.xml test`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Zero failures with real PostgreSQL fixtures.
- Fix: Reproduce smallest row pair; add a new migration or correct scoped query; preserve applied history.
- Verify: Run integrity and duplicate/concurrency scenarios.

## Client and contract disagree

- Symptom: Flutter/React parses wrong field or sees unexpected HTTP code.
- Likely cause: Stale mock/example, wrong base URL or changed token state.
- Diagnose: `flutter test`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Mock and live schema agree and token failure is explicit.
- Fix: Compare sole OpenAPI fixture to raw safe response; fix contract and both clients together.
- Verify: Run validation/unauthorized plus happy tests.

## Host or backup gate blocked

- Symptom: No confirmed real host/external disk, old dump, failed scratch restore.
- Likely cause: Production setup not ready, host sleeping, cron missed, disk unmounted or incompatible dump.
- Diagnose: `bash ops/restore-scratch.sh`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Scratch restore passes with recent verified external copy.
- Fix: Stop external exposure; check mount/age/major versions and recover in scratch only. Assign owner and cut stretch.
- Verify: Friday backup/restore and private deployed smoke must pass.

## Current mini-win fails

- Symptom: Live phone and React show same resources and recover after API errors.
- Likely cause: Implementation does not satisfy this week invariant or prerequisite.
- Diagnose: `bash scripts/acceptance/w08.sh diagnose`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: One minimal failing scenario with safe evidence or a documented healthy diagnostic.
- Fix: Use 45/90 minute protocol; preserve WIP, recover from last green branch, fix smallest test first.
- Verify: Re-run current feature matrix and regression before tag.

## Stop rule

[Stuck protocol](../STUCK-PROTOCOL.md) applies after 45 minutes. Never run destructive cleanup, disable tenant checks, or skip restore to manufacture a green gate.

# Week 03 verification and gate

> **Navigation:** [Previous: Week 02](../02-IDENTITY-AND-HOST/README.md) · [You are here](../YOU-ARE-HERE.md) · [Next: Week 04](../04-ATTENDANCE-CORE/README.md)

## Inspect first and build the test runner

The commands below target proposed `scripts/acceptance/w03.sh`, created in W03-S10 before execution. Each branch must execute a real JUnit/API or client assertion and propagate nonzero failure; an echo-only script is forbidden. Feature tests are added with their implementation steps, not postponed until Thursday. No runner or test is claimed to exist today.

Use two synthetic tenants, own/unrelated employees, direct-report manager and HR fixtures. Read auth tokens privately from test helpers; never put secrets in guide commands. For unavailable week-1 auth routes, unauthorized/cross-tenant cases assert diagnostic is private and DB tenant constraint fixtures; week 2 replaces those with authenticated API tests.

## Per-feature matrix

Repeat every case for each of this week first three stone outputs. Skip only if truly inapplicable and record why; critical path cases cannot be waved through.

| Case | Exact command after creation | Success looks like | Failure means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| happy | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh happy` | The three feature mini-wins above match their exact expected resource/state. | Owner route, state or setup is wrong. |
| validation | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh validation` | Malformed dates/empty required fields produce documented 400/422, no row. | DTO validation or domain rule missing. |
| unauthorized | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh unauthorized` | Missing/invalid token is 401; wrong role/hidden object 403/404. | Authentication or resource authorization defect. |
| cross-tenant | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh cross-tenant` | Tenant B identifiers expose no tenant A rows/counts/files. | Critical isolation defect; block gate. |
| duplicate | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh duplicate` | Same key returns same ID; changed body 409; one business effect. | Idempotency boundary is wrong. |
| concurrency | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh concurrency` | Concurrent same-employee/approval/balance commands preserve DB invariant. | Lock/unique/version rule is missing. |
| recovery | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh recovery` | Interrupted operation resumes or reconciles; no lost durable intent. | False success or incomplete recovery design. |
| integrity | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh integrity` | Tenant FK/unique/check constraints reject corrupt rows. | Database cannot defend invariant. |
| regression | `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh regression` | Previously green critical flows still pass. | New change broke baseline; recover before moving on. |

## Mini-win evidence

- [ ] Stone 1: Profile/admin form succeeds without broadening server authorization. Save request/test ID and actual safe output.
- [ ] Stone 2: Device/emulator and React show the same work date and grace rule. Save request/test ID and actual safe output.
- [ ] Stone 3: Before/after tests pass; no new production abstraction or accidental shared state. Save request/test ID and actual safe output.

- [ ] Required matrix cases executed with zero critical failures; regression reports saved.
- [ ] Migrations start clean, integrity checks pass, app starts and all five actual stone tags exist.
- [ ] Friday confirmed-host redeploy and authenticated smoke pass; week 1 local-only exception is recorded.
- [ ] External-copy backup and scratch restore verified; week 1 disposable local dump recorded.
- [ ] Global checklist evidence and dashboard updated; no critical failure silently omitted.

Result: **NOT RUN**. Record **PASS** only with all required evidence. **CONDITIONAL PASS** names noncritical outstanding item, owner and calendar due date. **FAIL** names critical check, minimal reproduction, recovery branch/tag and next action; that action becomes next week first stone before new scope.

# Week 03 troubleshooting

> **Navigation:** [Previous: Week 02](../02-IDENTITY-AND-HOST/README.md) · [You are here](../YOU-ARE-HERE.md) · [Next: Week 04](../04-ATTENDANCE-CORE/README.md)

## Runtime never becomes ready

- Symptom: Compose app unhealthy or request refuses connection.
- Likely cause: Docker stopped, wrong JDK, migration error or database not ready.
- Diagnose: `docker compose -f infra/selfhost/compose.yaml ps`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Healthy app and PostgreSQL with no public DB binding.
- Fix: Check disk then Docker/JDK; inspect last safe log lines; correct one config on branch, never delete volume.
- Verify: Re-run readiness and current happy scenario.

## Schema or key assertion fails

- Symptom: Migration/constraint/idempotency test returns an unexpected failure.
- Likely cause: Applied migration edited, missing tenant/key predicate or stale fixture.
- Diagnose: `mvn -f services/hrflow-app/pom.xml test`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Zero failures with real PostgreSQL fixtures.
- Fix: Reproduce smallest row pair; add a new migration or correct scoped query; preserve applied history.
- Verify: Run integrity and duplicate/concurrency scenarios.

## Client and contract disagree

- Symptom: Flutter/React parses wrong field or sees unexpected HTTP code.
- Likely cause: Stale mock/example, wrong base URL or changed token state.
- Diagnose: `flutter test`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Mock and live schema agree and token failure is explicit.
- Fix: Compare sole OpenAPI fixture to raw safe response; fix contract and both clients together.
- Verify: Run validation/unauthorized plus happy tests.

## Host or backup gate blocked

- Symptom: No confirmed real host/external disk, old dump, failed scratch restore.
- Likely cause: Production setup not ready, host sleeping, cron missed, disk unmounted or incompatible dump.
- Diagnose: `bash ops/restore-scratch.sh`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Scratch restore passes with recent verified external copy.
- Fix: Stop external exposure; check mount/age/major versions and recover in scratch only. Assign owner and cut stretch.
- Verify: Friday backup/restore and private deployed smoke must pass.

## Current mini-win fails

- Symptom: Profile/admin form succeeds without broadening server authorization.
- Likely cause: Implementation does not satisfy this week invariant or prerequisite.
- Diagnose: `bash scripts/acceptance/w03.sh diagnose`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: One minimal failing scenario with safe evidence or a documented healthy diagnostic.
- Fix: Use 45/90 minute protocol; preserve WIP, recover from last green branch, fix smallest test first.
- Verify: Re-run current feature matrix and regression before tag.

## Stop rule

[Stuck protocol](../STUCK-PROTOCOL.md) applies after 45 minutes. Never run destructive cleanup, disable tenant checks, or skip restore to manufacture a green gate.

## Objective and starting point

Build organization and admin as a visible mini-win. The audit found scaffolds, not this feature. Prerequisites are earlier green stones; none are pre-checked. Every named new path/class/script is a proposed implementation target: inspect for existing work first, then create only what is missing.

| 2 | Schedules and calendar | W03-S04 to S06 | 180 min, shared steps counted per owner |

## Minimum Viable Gate

- [ ] Profile/admin form succeeds without broadening server authorization.
- [ ] Device/emulator and React show the same work date and grace rule.
- [ ] Before/after tests pass; no new production abstraction or accidental shared state.
- [ ] Friday redeploy, authenticated smoke and scratch restore evidence exist.

## Stretch and exact cuts

- [ ] Improve wording/visual styling only if all critical tests are green.
- [ ] Add no more than the current lesson refactor after admission passes.

At 90 minutes stuck, simplify Stone 1 to one synthetic tenant and one happy-path fixture for diagnosis only; retain two-tenant security acceptance before the gate. Stone 2 drops optional filters/channels/extra forms, never locking or authorization. Stone 3 drops optional UI polish or pattern refactor and keeps the plain tested implementation. Stone 4 cuts all new scope. Stone 5 never skips backup/restore or substitutes a development machine for the agreed host.

## Friday demo and risks

I can demonstrate employees and hierarchy, schedules and calendar, and builder only after fixture pain. If prerequisites remain blocked, I show the failing check and recovery evidence instead of calling it done.

Main risks are missing prerequisites, unmeasured junior learning speed and host readiness. Do not start next week until this critical gate passes; when deadline pressure requires moving a noncritical item, record a conditional pass with owner/date and cut stretch first. No weekend work.

## Learn just in time

- [Repository](../primers/REPOSITORY.md).
- [Flyway](../primers/FLYWAY.md).
- [Builder](../primers/BUILDER.md).

Introduce at most two new concepts on any build day. Primers are 10 to 20 minutes; Thursday revises familiar concepts only. Required code/tests are not replaced by reading.

## Out of scope

Kafka runtime, ML, Kubernetes, cloud databases, tracking, new frameworks and unapproved patterns are excluded. A simpler tested switch beats an unadmitted abstraction.

# Week 02 verification and gate

> **Navigation:** [Previous: Week 01](../01-FOUNDATION/README.md) · [You are here](../YOU-ARE-HERE.md) · [Next: Week 03](../03-ORGANIZATION-AND-ADMIN/README.md)

## Inspect first and build the test runner

The commands below target proposed `scripts/acceptance/w02.sh`, created in W02-S12 before execution. Each branch must execute a real JUnit/API or client assertion and propagate nonzero failure; an echo-only script is forbidden. Feature tests are added with their implementation steps, not postponed until Thursday. No runner or test is claimed to exist today.

Use two synthetic tenants, own/unrelated employees, direct-report manager and HR fixtures. Read auth tokens privately from test helpers; never put secrets in guide commands. For unavailable week-1 auth routes, unauthorized/cross-tenant cases assert diagnostic is private and DB tenant constraint fixtures; week 2 replaces those with authenticated API tests.

## Per-feature matrix

Repeat every case for each of this week first three stone outputs. Skip only if truly inapplicable and record why; critical path cases cannot be waved through.

| Case | Exact command after creation | Success looks like | Failure means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| happy | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh happy` | The three feature mini-wins above match their exact expected resource/state. | Owner route, state or setup is wrong. |
| validation | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh validation` | Malformed dates/empty required fields produce documented 400/422, no row. | DTO validation or domain rule missing. |
| unauthorized | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh unauthorized` | Missing/invalid token is 401; wrong role/hidden object 403/404. | Authentication or resource authorization defect. |
| cross-tenant | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh cross-tenant` | Tenant B identifiers expose no tenant A rows/counts/files. | Critical isolation defect; block gate. |
| duplicate | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh duplicate` | Same key returns same ID; changed body 409; one business effect. | Idempotency boundary is wrong. |
| concurrency | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh concurrency` | Concurrent same-employee/approval/balance commands preserve DB invariant. | Lock/unique/version rule is missing. |
| recovery | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh recovery` | Interrupted operation resumes or reconciles; no lost durable intent. | False success or incomplete recovery design. |
| integrity | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh integrity` | Tenant FK/unique/check constraints reject corrupt rows. | Database cannot defend invariant. |
| regression | `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh regression` | Previously green critical flows still pass. | New change broke baseline; recover before moving on. |

## Mini-win evidence

- [ ] Stone 1: Own profile reload works; stale refresh forces login once. Save request/test ID and actual safe output.
- [ ] Stone 2: Both clients reject stale credentials and show safe errors. Save request/test ID and actual safe output.
- [ ] Stone 3: Scratch restore and login/profile smoke pass; source volume remains untouched. Save request/test ID and actual safe output.

## Minimum Viable Gate

- [ ] Required matrix cases executed with zero critical failures; regression reports saved.
- [ ] Migrations start clean, integrity checks pass, app starts and all five actual stone tags exist.
- [ ] Friday confirmed-host redeploy and authenticated smoke pass; week 1 local-only exception is recorded.
- [ ] External-copy backup and scratch restore verified; week 1 disposable local dump recorded.
- [ ] Global checklist evidence and dashboard updated; no critical failure silently omitted.

## Stretch

- [ ] Optional style/channel/refactor completed only after admission and full gate.

## Gate decision

Result: **NOT RUN**. Record **PASS** only with all required evidence. **CONDITIONAL PASS** names noncritical outstanding item, owner and calendar due date. **FAIL** names critical check, minimal reproduction, recovery branch/tag and next action; that action becomes next week first stone before new scope.

## Retro

- What was slow: actual step ID, elapsed time, and why.
- What to cut: named stretch item; never security or restore tests.
- Energy: rested, steady, tired, or stop; protect weekend.
- Pattern review: admission answers, simpler alternative, and whether it was worth it.
- Next week: hours confirmed, carried failure owner, and exact first action.

# Week 02 troubleshooting

> **Navigation:** [Previous: Week 01](../01-FOUNDATION/README.md) · [You are here](../YOU-ARE-HERE.md) · [Next: Week 03](../03-ORGANIZATION-AND-ADMIN/README.md)

## Runtime never becomes ready

- Symptom: Compose app unhealthy or request refuses connection.
- Likely cause: Docker stopped, wrong JDK, migration error or database not ready.
- Diagnose: `docker compose -f infra/selfhost/compose.yaml ps`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Healthy app and PostgreSQL with no public DB binding.
- Fix: Check disk then Docker/JDK; inspect last safe log lines; correct one config on branch, never delete volume.
- Verify: Re-run readiness and current happy scenario.

## Schema or key assertion fails

- Symptom: Migration/constraint/idempotency test returns an unexpected failure.
- Likely cause: Applied migration edited, missing tenant/key predicate or stale fixture.
- Diagnose: `mvn -f services/hrflow-app/pom.xml test`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Zero failures with real PostgreSQL fixtures.
- Fix: Reproduce smallest row pair; add a new migration or correct scoped query; preserve applied history.
- Verify: Run integrity and duplicate/concurrency scenarios.

## Client and contract disagree

- Symptom: Flutter/React parses wrong field or sees unexpected HTTP code.
- Likely cause: Stale mock/example, wrong base URL or changed token state.
- Diagnose: `flutter test`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Mock and live schema agree and token failure is explicit.
- Fix: Compare sole OpenAPI fixture to raw safe response; fix contract and both clients together.
- Verify: Run validation/unauthorized plus happy tests.

## Host or backup gate blocked

- Symptom: No confirmed real host/external disk, old dump, failed scratch restore.
- Likely cause: Production setup not ready, host sleeping, cron missed, disk unmounted or incompatible dump.
- Diagnose: `bash ops/restore-scratch.sh`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: Scratch restore passes with recent verified external copy.
- Fix: Stop external exposure; check mount/age/major versions and recover in scratch only. Assign owner and cut stretch.
- Verify: Friday backup/restore and private deployed smoke must pass.

## Current mini-win fails

- Symptom: Own profile reload works; stale refresh forces login once.
- Likely cause: Implementation does not satisfy this week invariant or prerequisite.
- Diagnose: `bash scripts/acceptance/w02.sh diagnose`; inspect target first, because scripts are proposed until their build step.
- Healthy result: One minimal failing scenario with safe evidence or a documented healthy diagnostic.
- Fix: Use 45/90 minute protocol; preserve WIP, recover from last green branch, fix smallest test first.
- Verify: Re-run current feature matrix and regression before tag.

## Stop rule

[Stuck protocol](../STUCK-PROTOCOL.md) applies after 45 minutes. Never run destructive cleanup, disable tenant checks, or skip restore to manufacture a green gate.

> **Navigation:** [Previous: Week 01](../01-FOUNDATION/README.md) · [You are here](../YOU-ARE-HERE.md) · [Next: Week 03](../03-ORGANIZATION-AND-ADMIN/README.md)

## At a glance

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Week | 02 |
| Owners | A backend/web/infra; B Flutter and client acceptance |
| Planned maximum | A 16.8 h, B 16.8 h; 70 percent of 24, light-week reduction where applicable |
| Depends on | Week 01 critical gate or its explicit carried failure |
| Gate | **NOT RUN** |

## Objective and starting point

Build identity and private host deployment as a visible mini-win. The audit found scaffolds, not this feature. Prerequisites are earlier green stones; none are pre-checked. Every named new path/class/script is a proposed implementation target: inspect for existing work first, then create only what is missing.

## Stepping stones

| Stone | Visible win | Steps | Upper step time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Credentials and tenant context | W02-S01 to S05 | 300 min, shared steps counted per owner |
| 2 | Isolation before exposure | W02-S06 to S08 | 180 min, shared steps counted per owner |
| 3 | The skeleton reaches the real host | W02-S09 to S11 | 180 min, shared steps counted per owner |
| 4 | Buffer evidence and failure recovery | W02-S12 to S14 | 180 min, shared steps counted per owner |
| 5 | Friday gate deploy and recovery | W02-S15 to S17 | 180 min, shared steps counted per owner |

## Minimum Viable Gate

- [ ] Own profile reload works; stale refresh forces login once.
- [ ] Both clients reject stale credentials and show safe errors.
- [ ] Scratch restore and login/profile smoke pass; source volume remains untouched.
- [ ] Friday redeploy, authenticated smoke and scratch restore evidence exist.
- [ ] Security/correctness/event/restore failures are fixed or this critical gate stays **FAIL**.

## Stretch and exact cuts

- [ ] Improve wording/visual styling only if all critical tests are green.
- [ ] Add no more than the current lesson refactor after admission passes.

At 90 minutes stuck, simplify Stone 1 to one synthetic tenant and one happy-path fixture for diagnosis only; retain two-tenant security acceptance before the gate. Stone 2 drops optional filters/channels/extra forms, never locking or authorization. Stone 3 drops optional UI polish or pattern refactor and keeps the plain tested implementation. Stone 4 cuts all new scope. Stone 5 never skips backup/restore or substitutes a development machine for the agreed host.

## Friday demo and risks

I can demonstrate credentials and tenant context, isolation before exposure, and the skeleton reaches the real host. If prerequisites remain blocked, I show the failing check and recovery evidence instead of calling it done.

Main risks are missing prerequisites, unmeasured junior learning speed and host readiness. Do not start next week until this critical gate passes; when deadline pressure requires moving a noncritical item, record a conditional pass with owner/date and cut stretch first. No weekend work.

## Learn just in time

- [Jwt Refresh](../primers/JWT-REFRESH.md).
- [Multi Tenancy](../primers/MULTI-TENANCY.md).
- [Backups Restores](../primers/BACKUPS-RESTORES.md).
- [Reverse Proxy Https](../primers/REVERSE-PROXY-HTTPS.md).
- [Tunnels](../primers/TUNNELS.md).

Introduce at most two new concepts on any build day. Primers are 10 to 20 minutes; Thursday revises familiar concepts only. Required code/tests are not replaced by reading.

## Out of scope

Kafka runtime, ML, Kubernetes, cloud databases, tracking, new frameworks and unapproved patterns are excluded. A simpler tested switch beats an unadmitted abstraction.

# Private host and tunnel access setup

## Preconditions and safe order

Production setup is not ready. First confirm the exact host, at least 30 GiB free, Docker runtime, domain/DNS control, external encrypted disk and operator. Complete W02 security tests and restore before enabling a public hostname. Until then deploy loopback/private LAN only and mark external access **FAIL**. Never forward router ports or publish database/monitoring administration.

## Caddy is the application gateway

Create proposed `infra/selfhost/Caddyfile`. This private origin example assumes the new app listens on internal 8080 and React production files are mounted read-only under `/srv/web`. It is not a config already present in the repository.

```text
http://:80 {
    handle /api/* {
        reverse_proxy app:8080
    }
    handle {
        root * /srv/web
        try_files {path} /index.html
        file_server
    }
}
```

Only cloudflared and approved internal clients can reach the origin network in public tunnel mode. Do not route Actuator/diagnostic/admin paths through the public proxy. Validate upstream auth and resource authorization with direct API attempts; static navigation hiding is not security. Add response security headers and explicit body/time limits in the tested deployment config before public release.

## Configure outbound access

1. Use the owned domain in Cloudflare DNS; verify current plan/registrar terms and actual annual price privately. Tunnel publishing itself does not require a paid Access plan.
1. Create a named Tunnel in the account you control. Copy connector credentials into a private host secret file with restrictive permissions, never Git or this guide.
1. Add cloudflared to the private Caddy network only, with restart/log bounds. Use the provider's documented token-file mechanism for the chosen locked image version; inspect its help before configuring secrets. Do not print the token in command history or Compose rendered output.
1. Map only the application hostname to `http://caddy:80`; no Docker/Kuma/PostgreSQL/Kafka routes. Public HTTPS terminates automatically at Cloudflare; origin is private HTTP. Do not claim a Caddy ACME certificate was issued in this mode.
1. Before enabling the hostname, rerun security, firewall/published-port, secrets-redaction and external-copy restore gates. Test invalid/missing tokens and cross-tenant IDs from a phone on a different network.
1. Enable only the approved hostname; inspect the browser certificate and confirmed issuer/expiry. Test refresh cookies/origins/CORS on the exact hostname, not merely localhost.
1. Disable connector and confirm remote access fails while local data/private authenticated access remain intact. Record ISP/provider dependency and restart behavior.

Use the official [Tunnel setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/) and [publishing guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/routing-to-tunnel/) for current dashboard terminology. Their UI can change; verify in your account rather than following invented screenshots.

## Week 2 host gate

- [ ] Private confirmed-host skeleton redeployed, not merely development localhost.
- [ ] Auth/tenant/resource tests and rotating refresh tests pass.
- [ ] HTTPS certificate/origin flow is verified before external access.
- [ ] Firewall/private networks expose none of database, Docker or monitoring administration.
- [ ] Encrypted external copy and scratch restore pass before hostname goes live.
- [ ] Unknown domain/router/host issues have owner and recovery action; remote gate stays **FAIL**.

## Friday repeat

Run the deployment manifest/smoke script on the real host with the exact checked image. Preserve previous digest/config and test a known authenticated request from React and Flutter. Backup/restore still run when remote access is blocked; label private versus public result separately. Complete final operational drills with the Week 10 host runbook.
